a51.speaker: Eliseu Tavares, President of Siscap
a51.name: Eliseu Tavares
a51.title: President of Siscap
a51.speech: Said that the Sotavento Court of Appeal had upheld the judgement handed down by the Praia District Court, considering all the alleged facts about the challenge to the meeting of the National Council of the UNTC-CS to be proven. Considered that the judgement was "yet another fraud, yet another illegality practised by the secretary general of the UNTC-CS," Joaquina Almeida. Stated that the court considered all the allegations, noting that two lists were voted on at the 2016 Congress, both of which elected members to the National Council, and that the lists included the names of the members of each list.

a51.speaker: Trade Union Platform - Unite and Rescue the UNTC-CS
a51.name: Trade Union Platform - Unite and Rescue the UNTC-CS
a51.speech: Celebrated "with confidence in justice, another victory" in the process of challenging the alleged meeting of the National Council of the UNTC-CS.

a113.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a113.name: Olavo Correia
a113.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a113.speech: "I want to tell you that we had a meeting today, this morning, about this partnership between the United States and Cabo Verde, through this new compact," emphasising the values shared by the two nations, including democracy, freedom, human dignity and peace, and saying the partnership goes beyond economic agreements, being an alliance anchored in fundamental principles.

a113.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a113.name: Olavo Correia
a113.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a113.speech: Outlined priority areas for cooperation, including connectivity, energy transition, education and diversified economic development, and stressed the importance of investment in human capital and in creating opportunities for young people and women ; "We are committed to working at this stage to put this new compact at the service of Cabo Verde's accelerated economic growth" ; acknowledged the need to align the new compact with Cabo Verde's long-term development strategies and reiterated the mutual commitment of both nations to achieving tangible and significant results.

a113.speaker: Alice Albright, Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a113.name: Alice Albright
a113.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a113.speech: Highlighted the history of cooperation between the United States and Cabo Verde, praising the country for its commitment to democratic principles, human rights and economic development: "Cabo Verde, for us at the MCC and for us in the United States, continues to be a leader, demonstrating how well-elected modern democracies deliver results. Cabo Verde delivered. It complied with responsibility. It respected human rights, the rule of law, not only in the West and, frankly, throughout the world."

a113.speaker: Alice Albright, Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a113.name: Alice Albright
a113.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a113.speech: Said the new regional compact will focus on regional integration, opportunity and the future, and stressed that Cabo Verde will be the first island country to take part in a regional compact with the MCC: "This compact will focus on regional integration, on opportunity and on the future, in line with some of the wonderful aspects of the vision that the Vice-President outlined. Regional compacts are a new opportunity for us and this is the first time we will be working with an island nation. So we are very excited to have the opportunity to experiment with you and test new things in this area."

a284.speaker: Senators Amara M. Konneh (Gbarpolu County), Edwin M. Snowe (Bomi County), Gbezhongar M. Findley (Grand Bassa County) and Augustine Chea (Sinoe County) (joint communication to the Liberian Senate)
a284.name: Senators Amara M. Konneh (Gbarpolu County)
a284.title: Edwin M. Snowe (Bomi County), Gbezhongar M. Findley (Grand Bassa County) and Augustine Chea (Sinoe County) (joint communication to the Liberian Senate)
a284.speech: Raised concern in a communication alarming of a potential collapse of key sectors and shortfall of the 2025 National budget because of programs supported by the United States Government through USAID, naming Education, Health and Agriculture as major sectors in the country that risk major collapse and setback due to the aid suspension by the Trump Administration.

a284.speaker: Amara M. Konneh, Senator of Gbarpolu County and Chairman of Public Accounts at the Liberian Senate
a284.name: Amara M. Konneh
a284.title: Senator of Gbarpolu County and Chairman of Public Accounts at the Liberian Senate
a284.speech: Said that the situation requires a thoughtful reassessment of government's budgeting and development financing strategies and priorities for the coming four years ; "Considering United States President Donald Trump's recent policy to temporarily suspend a significant portion of foreign assistance as part of his "America First" initiative, resulting in the pause of billions of dollars in global funding, pending a 90-day review by the State Department - it is crucial to acknowledge that the Government of Liberia faces a significant underlying challenge that necessitates our immediate attention".

a284.speaker: Amara M. Konneh, Senator of Gbarpolu County
a284.name: Amara M. Konneh
a284.title: Senator of Gbarpolu County
a284.speech: Reflected that in 2024 the United States and Liberia formalized Amendments 14 and 15 to the Development Objective agreement initially established in May 2020 with the former CDC-led administration, and indicated that the agreement entails an additional investment of US$114,488,125.00, which accounts for approximately 14 percent of Liberia's national budget ; says, as articulated by USAID, that the primary aim of this off-budget funding is to enhance development initiatives in Liberia, particularly in health, education and economic growth ; "This strategic support is designed to foster essential reforms and cultivate a healthy and educated workforce, thereby paving the way for sustainable development in the nation. Before the implementation of the freeze, USAID was actively engaged in several vital programs in Liberia that assisted the government in meeting the needs of its people".

a284.speaker: Amara M. Konneh, Senator of Gbarpolu County and Chairman of Public Accounts
a284.name: Amara M. Konneh
a284.title: Senator of Gbarpolu County and Chairman of Public Accounts
a284.speech: Noted that the recent announcement regarding the United States' suspension of foreign aid presents considerable challenges to Liberia's important initiatives focused on enhancing its public health, education and agriculture sectors, saying these initiatives are crucial for providing essential medications to children and individuals facing serious health conditions, sustaining educational programs for students, and addressing serious food insecurity and jobs in the agriculture sector ; warned of possible disruptions in hospital supplies, interruptions to school feeding programs, and insufficient support for essential services in the coming 90 days ; lamented that the Liberian Senate must ensure prioritization of stable funding allocations to safeguard continuity of these vital programs and mitigate any potential negative impacts on the Government of Liberia's development agenda.

a284.speaker: Amara M. Konneh, Senator and former Minister of Finance
a284.name: Amara M. Konneh
a284.title: Senator and former Minister of Finance
a284.speech: "To enhance the Liberian Senate's understanding of the potential implications stemming from the suspension of US foreign assistance, we respectfully recommend that the Committee on Ways, Means, and Finance, along with the Committee on Foreign Affairs, consider inviting the Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Finance and Development Planning, Health and Social Welfare, Education, and Agriculture to provide a briefing this week" ; believes such a discussion would be invaluable in assessing the socio-economic challenges this policy may pose for Liberia and identifying strategic avenues through which the Senate can support the Executive Branch in mitigating any adverse effects.

a284.speaker: Senators' communication (conclusion)
a284.name: Senators' communication (conclusion)
a284.speech: "We look forward to your and our colleagues' favorable consideration of this proposal. Please accept, Madam Pro-Tempore, the assurances of our highest esteem".

a313.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a313.name: Antonio Guterres
a313.title: UN Secretary-General
a313.speech: “We need peace everywhere. We need peace in Gaza with an immediate ceasefire and an immediate and unconditional release of all the hostages,” said during the BRICS meeting in Kazan ; said it was necessary to distribute humanitarian aid effectively and to make “irreversible” progress towards “ending the Israeli occupation” and implementing the two-State solution.

a313.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a313.name: Antonio Guterres
a313.title: UN Secretary-General
a313.speech: “We need peace in Lebanon, with an immediate cessation of hostilities, advancing towards the full implementation of Security Council resolution 1701.”

a313.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a313.name: Antonio Guterres
a313.title: UN Secretary-General
a313.speech: Called, on Russian soil, for peace in Ukraine: “A just peace, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, international law and the resolutions of the General Assembly.”

a313.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a313.name: Antonio Guterres
a313.title: UN Secretary-General
a313.speech: Called for an agreement in Sudan and for the defence of “the values of the Charter of the United Nations, of the rule of law and of the principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of all States.”

a313.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a313.name: Antonio Guterres
a313.title: UN Secretary-General
a313.speech: Recalled the four challenges the Summit of the Future set out for finance, climate, technology and peace, concluding: “The Summit of the Future marked the path towards reinforcing multilateralism, towards global development and security. Now we must turn words into actions.”

a451.speaker: Health experts
a451.name: Health experts
a451.speech: Are raising concerns over the growing threat of hepatitis in the country and warn that hepatitis remains a silent killer in South Sudan, despite being preventable through vaccination and treatable if detected early ; say Hepatitis B is mostly spread through blood contact, unprotected sex, mother-to-child transmission during delivery, and sharing sharp objects like needles and razors, while Hepatitis A and E are mainly linked to contaminated food and water and Hepatitis D only occurs alongside Hepatitis B.

a451.speaker: Matiok Anthony, Executive Director of Friends of Humanity
a451.name: Matiok Anthony
a451.title: Executive Director of Friends of Humanity
a451.speech: Says the disease is often unnoticed until it’s too late: “Hepatitis is a silent killer because its early signs like fatigue, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite are similar to common illnesses. The only way to know your status is through testing” ; warns that cultural practices such as traditional scarification, communal use of sharp objects, and poor infection control have fuelled transmission ; highlights that newborn babies from infected mothers face a 90% risk of developing chronic hepatitis without timely vaccination: “The first dose of Hepatitis B vaccine should be given within 24 hours of birth, but South Sudan still lacks this birth dose vaccine”.

a451.speaker: Matiok Anthony, Executive Director of Friends of Humanity
a451.name: Matiok Anthony
a451.title: Executive Director of Friends of Humanity
a451.speech: Urged, on the organisation’s $2 fundraising initiative to establish a Hepatitis Treatment Center at Juba Teaching Hospital: “Hepatitis doesn’t attract donor funding like HIV or malaria. We need citizens to take the lead know your status, get vaccinated, and support this initiative”.

a451.speaker: Global health reports (cited)
a451.name: Global health reports (cited)
a451.speech: According to global health reports, South Sudan faces high prevalence rates of 9.9% for Hepatitis B and 9.1% for Hepatitis C.

a451.speaker: Dr. Ambrose Anthony, medical doctor
a451.name: Dr. Ambrose Anthony
a451.title: medical doctor
a451.speech: Explains that hepatitis primarily affects the liver and can go unnoticed until severe damage occurs: “Hepatitis is a disease of the liver and it’s like a silent killer. Most people don’t know they have it until symptoms appear” ; says the early signs include persistent fatigue and weakness, yellowing of the eyes (jaundice), dark-coloured urine, abdominal pain and sometimes fever: “These are the major symptoms that signal hepatitis infection” ; says hepatitis is a viral disease transmitted mainly through infected blood and body fluids, including unprotected sex, sharing needles, exposure to infected blood or vomit, and mother-to-child transmission during childbirth.

a451.speaker: Dr. Ambrose Anthony, medical doctor
a451.name: Dr. Ambrose Anthony
a451.title: medical doctor
a451.speech: Warns that “Some young people engage in unprotected sex or share sharp objects like needles. These behaviours make them highly vulnerable” ; explains that one of the biggest misconceptions is that a vaccine can cure hepatitis after infection: “If you already have hepatitis, taking a vaccine will not help. It only adds more load on your body. Vaccination is for prevention, not treatment” ; emphasizes early screening as the most effective preventive measure: “Know your status. If you test negative, take the vaccine. If positive, start treatment immediately to avoid complications” ; “Screen yourself. Know your status. Take the vaccine if negative, and if positive, seek treatment immediately. Hepatitis is dangerous, but together we can defeat it”.

a451.speaker: Dr. Ambrose Anthony, medical doctor
a451.name: Dr. Ambrose Anthony
a451.title: medical doctor
a451.speech: Calls for collaborative action between citizens, health workers, and the government: “If the community pushes for services, the government will prioritize them. Eliminating hepatitis needs strategy, planning, and awareness” ; appeals for behavioural change among youth: “Use condoms during sex and avoid sharing needles. Prevention is easier and cheaper than treatment” ; says “More than 95% of hepatitis cases can clear naturally if detected early and monitored. But late detection leads to chronic infection and complications”.

a648.speaker: Brereton Mitambo, head of administration, Emmanuel International
a648.name: Brereton Mitambo
a648.title: head of administration, Emmanuel International
a648.speech: “Our mission is built on the understanding that development is sustainable only if it’s driven by the local community. Our focus on capacity-building and community empowerment has enabled rural Malawians to take ownership of their development, leading to lasting impact.” ; “Our partnerships with donors, government agencies and local structures amplify our impact. Together, we’ve changed thousands of lives.”

a648.speaker: Nicholas Balazani, farmer from Ntanga Village, T/A Jalasi, Mangochi
a648.name: Nicholas Balazani
a648.title: farmer from Ntanga Village, T/A Jalasi, Mangochi
a648.speech: says he and his wife have learnt new farming methods that have increased their maize harvest from 15 bags to 26-40 bags per acre: “We used to harvest just enough for consumption, but now we have a surplus to sell. The training we received through the Titukulane project has made a huge difference in our lives.” ; “We are proud of what we have achieved. We are now food-secure and our children are attending school.”

a648.speaker: Sofia Balazani, farmer from Ntanga Village, T/A Jalasi, Mangochi
a648.name: Sofia Balazani
a648.title: farmer from Ntanga Village, T/A Jalasi, Mangochi
a648.speech: “Joining the village savings and loans association has also helped us manage our finances better. We make joint decisions on investments and have seen significant improvements in our financial status.”

a648.speaker: Charles Mukiwa, country director of Emmanuel International
a648.name: Charles Mukiwa
a648.title: country director of Emmanuel International
a648.speech: says EI remains committed to accelerating rural development: “We will continue to serve the country, helping to conquer food insecurity, supporting the health sector, agriculture, entrepreneurship, clean water and many more areas. We believe that together, we can help Malawi achieve its vision of becoming a prosperous nation by 2063.”

a648.speaker: SOCO/Titukulane project implementers and EI booklet (report)
a648.name: SOCO/Titukulane project implementers and EI booklet (report)
a648.speech: Recently published a booklet celebrating four years of success in women’s economic empowerment, youth skills development, food security and climate change adaptation under the Titukulane Project, reporting that the USAid-funded Titukulane project supported over 5,000 women and youth in Mangochi to establish thriving small businesses.

a780.speaker: Dr. Taiwo Johnson, TCI Nigeria Country Director
a780.name: Dr. Taiwo Johnson
a780.title: TCI Nigeria Country Director
a780.speech: Announced during a stakeholders' meeting that The Challenge Initiative had formally handed over its family planning programme to the Edo government; noted that the handover marked a significant milestone in their journey with the Edo government, which started over three and a half years ago, and described the moment as a transitioning point signalling a shift in responsibility from TCI to the government for all family planning activities in the state: "Now that we are transitioning to self-reliance, we expect Edo to take complete ownership of all family planning activities" ; stated that although TCI 2.0 was coming to a close, a new version was expected in 2026, with modalities still under discussion; commended the Edo State Ministry of Health and staff for their support.

a780.speaker: Dr. Taiwo Johnson, TCI Nigeria Country Director
a780.name: Dr. Taiwo Johnson
a780.title: TCI Nigeria Country Director
a780.speech: Noted that global funding for family planning had reduced, referencing the withdrawal of support by major partners like USAID and other international donors; revealed that, unlike 2024, the state has not secured any funding for family planning in 2025, stressing that the gap must be addressed urgently ; "No product, no service, even with training, demand generation, and media support, if commodities are not available, family planning services will fail." ; "Family planning is critical. If properly implemented, it can reduce maternal mortality by as much as 30 percent"

a780.speaker: Dr Cyril Oshiomhole, Edo State Commissioner for Health
a780.name: Dr Cyril Oshiomhole
a780.title: Edo State Commissioner for Health
a780.speech: Commended TCI efforts at addressing a critical gap in the state public health landscape and emphasised that with focused intervention in nine local government areas, TCI has helped Edo improve service delivery and build the capacity of health workers: "We have seen a measurable increase in contraceptive pre-balance, a stronger referral system, and an encouraging reduction in the unmet need for family planning services. We have witnessed a shift in communities towards accepting and owning their reproductive choices guided by accurate information and data. TCI may be closing shop in terms of direct implementation. But, the seeds they have planted will continue to yield results for years to come. Let us continue to champion the message that family planning is not a health issue. It is a development tool."

a795.speaker: Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila, Speaker of the Namibian National Assembly
a795.name: Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila
a795.title: Speaker of the Namibian National Assembly
a795.speech: Reiterated the call for greater global commitment to humanitarian assistance and the protection of human rights during the Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly in Geneva ; "Although we have international conventions that unite us as a global community to provide humanitarian assistance to those affected by crises, we are not fully living up to the commitments we have made. Many communities remain in dire straits, without the necessary assistance, and continue to face human rights violations." ; said the conference agreed that there is a need to ensure compliance with humanitarian obligations and equitable resource sharing, including capacity building to reach affected communities.

a795.speaker: Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly (conference)
a795.name: Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly (conference)
a795.speech: Noted with concern the rise in humanitarian crises worldwide, despite existing international conventions meant to address such challenges; the Assembly also discussed the persistent exclusion of women from political decision-making processes.

a795.speaker: Delegates at the IPU Assembly
a795.name: Delegates at the IPU Assembly
a795.speech: Underscored the need to mainstream gender equality into national policies and laws to ensure that women's voices and perspectives are included in shaping governance and development priorities.

a795.speaker: Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila, Speaker of the Namibian National Assembly
a795.name: Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila
a795.title: Speaker of the Namibian National Assembly
a795.speech: "We also agreed to ensure that we learn from each other, and we have developed tools that we have agreed to utilise to ensure that we develop the human capacity that women possess. The African group also drew the attention of the IPU to the situation in Madagascar, which is a deviation from the norms that we have adopted as an African continent, and it called on the IPU to support the efforts of the continent to help that country to revert back to democracy, which is the governance system that we have adopted for the African continent."

a795.speaker: Namibian delegation to the IPU Assembly
a795.name: Namibian delegation to the IPU Assembly
a795.speech: Used the platform to call for an end to the economic blockade against Cuba and the sanctions imposed on Venezuela; the delegation further expressed solidarity with the people of Palestine, calling on the international community to support their right to self-determination and to end ongoing human rights violations in the region.

a831.speaker: Ethiopia Education Cluster report (comprising the Ministry of Education, Save the Children and UNICEF)
a831.name: Ethiopia Education Cluster report (comprising the Ministry of Education
a831.title: Save the Children and UNICEF)
a831.speech: Recent data revealed massive damage to schools across conflict-affected areas of Tigray, Amhara and Afar in northern Ethiopia, with the situation particularly bad in Tigray, where 85% of schools have serious or partial damage and all public schools remain closed; reported that 2.3 million children in the region have been out of school for around three years as a result of the COVID pandemic followed by two years of conflict, and that 22,500 teachers have gone without pay for more than two years.

a831.speaker: Zinash, 13, fifth-grade student at a primary school in Ethiopia’s Amhara region
a831.name: Zinash
a831.title: 13, fifth-grade student at a primary school in Ethiopia’s Amhara region
a831.speech: “A year ago, my family and I ran from our village escaping the fighting that broke out here. Houses were destroyed by the conflict and properties were damaged and many people had to flee the area. Now after almost a year, I am able to continue my education and I am in grade five at a nearby primary school.”

a831.speaker: Xavier Joubert, Save the Children’s Country Director for Ethiopia
a831.name: Xavier Joubert
a831.title: Save the Children’s Country Director for Ethiopia
a831.speech: “The current humanitarian crisis in Ethiopia is one of the worst in recent memory. Conflict, hunger and the impact of the climate crisis have forced millions from their homes, resulting in countless children being forced to drop out of school. It’s essential that school buildings which have been damaged or destroyed by the conflict are fixed, and that unpaid teachers receive an incentive for their work. We are supporting children affected by the conflict to continue learning, but more needs to be done to ensure every last child affected by the humanitarian crisis, including conflict, has access to an education.”

a831.speaker: Save the Children (statement)
a831.name: Save the Children (statement)
a831.speech: Said it is running safe spaces where children can receive emotional support and are encouraged to express their feelings through games and role play, and is also providing books and other learning materials to help children go back to school, but that more needs to be done to meet people’s humanitarian needs, including children’s education; noted that a UN appeal for Ethiopia is only 18.4% funded, meaning an additional $3.26 billion USD is desperately needed, and that in 2022 Save the Children reached about 7.6 million people including about 5.1 million children.

a889.speaker: A.M. Evstigneeva, Russian Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a889.name: A.M. Evstigneeva
a889.title: Russian Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a889.speech: Said the past period has been accompanied by active electoral processes at the national level, noting the intensive electoral campaigns in Ghana, Senegal, Cape Verde and Guinea-Bissau, which are generally peaceful and orderly, and that constitutional reforms are progressing successfully in the Gambia, Togo and Sierra Leone; said the situation at the regional level is characterized by the reorganization of cooperation between the countries of the region and the search for new ways of interaction, and expressed satisfaction with the establishment of new economic ties between individual countries of the Sahel and the Gulf of Guinea, hoping that such examples will set the tone for the development of good-neighborly and mutually beneficial relations in the long term.

a889.speaker: A.M. Evstigneeva, Russian Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a889.name: A.M. Evstigneeva
a889.title: Russian Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a889.speech: Said the security situation continues to be characterized by the increasing activity of numerous terrorist and criminal groups, and that “all this is a heavy burden of consequences of the military aggression of Western countries against Libya, which all the states of the region continue to bear today”; said the most difficult situation is observed in the Liptako-Gurma triangle, where the activity of the Al-Qaeda-affiliated “Islam and Muslim Support Group” and the “Islamic State in the Greater Sahara” is high, and that the strengthening of the Islamic State’s combat potential in West Africa complicates the security situation in the countries of the Lake Chad basin.

a889.speaker: A.M. Evstigneeva, Russian Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a889.name: A.M. Evstigneeva
a889.title: Russian Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a889.speech: Said long-term stabilization in the Sahara-Sahel requires the support of the international community for Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, which have become the vanguard of the fight against trans-African terrorist groups, noting the success of their operations and the close coordination of efforts, including in the field of mutual transfer of operational data and intelligence.

a889.speaker: A.M. Evstigneeva, Russian Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a889.name: A.M. Evstigneeva
a889.title: Russian Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a889.speech: Said Russia will continue to make a constructive contribution to collective efforts aimed at achieving stability in the Sahara-Sahel and West Africa as a whole, and will continue to provide support to the States of the subregion on a bilateral basis, citing as an example the agreement reached in September between Roscosmos Corporation and the countries of the Sahel Alliance of States on the launch of a communications satellite and an Earth remote sensing satellite; said Russia will continue to support the countries of the region in improving the combat capability of the national armed forces, training military personnel and law enforcement officers, and intends to expand the volume of humanitarian assistance provided.

a937.speaker: Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.name: Nasser Bourita
a937.title: Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.speech: Stated on Thursday that Morocco rejects the logic of “crisis management” in the face of Israeli measures deemed unacceptable, and that it will continue to give priority to peace as a “strategic choice” under the leadership of King Mohammed VI ; stressed that Rabat intends to pursue its diplomatic efforts in order to bring together the conditions conducive to a return to negotiations, the only path capable of leading to a definitive solution and of guaranteeing stability in the Middle East.

a937.speaker: Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.name: Nasser Bourita
a937.title: Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.speech: Reiterated Morocco's call for an immediate ceasefire in the Palestinian territories, for the opening of all crossing points to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza, and for the preservation of UNRWA's role; denounced the demolition of houses and the expulsion of civilians in the West Bank, as well as violations of the status quo in Jerusalem, calling on the international community to act urgently.

a937.speaker: Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.name: Nasser Bourita
a937.title: Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.speech: Recalled that King Mohammed VI, as chairman of the Al-Quds Committee, had recently ordered the dispatch of 300 tonnes of foodstuffs, medicines and humanitarian aid to Gaza, while continuing, through the Bayt Mal Al-Quds Acharif Agency, programmes intended to support the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to protect the historic and religious status of the city.

a937.speaker: Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.name: Nasser Bourita
a937.title: Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.speech: Welcomed the international momentum in favour of the recognition of the Palestinian State and recalled that Rabat had co-organised with The Hague the fifth meeting of the International Alliance for the Two-State Solution; confirmed the reopening of Morocco's embassy in Damascus, with the aim of strengthening relations with Syria and supporting its political process.

a937.speaker: Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.name: Nasser Bourita
a937.title: Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a937.speech: Insisted on the need for a rapid reform of the Arab League so that it can fulfil its role in terms of solidarity, unity and the defence of the collective interests of the Arab peoples.

a1001.name: Elon Musk
a1001.title: businessman, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a1001.speech: Said that President Donald Trump had agreed to shut down USAID; said today that he had spoken to Trump about the US aid and development agency, which has existed for six decades.

a1001.speaker: 600 USAID employees
a1001.name: 600 USAID employees
a1001.speech: Said they had been blocked from the computer system.

a1001.speaker: USAID Agency leadership (email to staff)
a1001.name: USAID Agency leadership (email to staff)
a1001.speech: Those still in the system received emails saying that "under the direction of Agency leadership" the headquarters building "will be closed to Agency personnel on Monday, 3 February".

a1001.speaker: Musk, Trump and some Republican members of Congress
a1001.name: Musk
a1001.title: Trump and some Republican members of Congress
a1001.speech: Have criticised USAID, which oversees humanitarian, development and security programmes in about 120 countries, in increasingly harsh terms, accusing it of promoting progressive causes.

a1001.speaker: Washington Post
a1001.name: Washington Post
a1001.speech: Reported that a senior Treasury official had resigned because Musk's team had gained access to confidential information.

a1001.speaker: Democratic members of Congress
a1001.name: Democratic members of Congress
a1001.speech: Protested against the measures, saying that Trump does not have the constitutional authority to shut down USAID without the approval of Congress, and condemned Musk's access to confidential information held by the government.

a1001.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1001.name: Donald Trump
a1001.title: US President
a1001.speech: "It's run by a bunch of radical lunatics. And we're getting them out of there," Trump explained to journalists about USAID on Sunday night.

a1001.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a1001.name: Marco Rubio
a1001.title: US Secretary of State
a1001.speech: Has not spoken publicly about any plan to close USAID.

a1002.speaker: USAID Afya Yangu (My Health) Southern and USAID Kizazi Hodari (Brave Generation) Southern Zone projects, under Deloitte Consulting Limited
a1002.name: USAID Afya Yangu (My Health) Southern and USAID Kizazi Hodari (Brave Generation) Southern Zone projects
a1002.title: under Deloitte Consulting Limited
a1002.speech: Have announced a provision of a well-coordinated HIV services during the celebrations ahead of the climax of World AIDS Day 2024 which will be held in Songea, Ruvuma region on Sunday December 1st.

a1002.speaker: Dr George Sikalengo, Regional Technical Lead for AIDS, USAID Afya Yangu Southern Project
a1002.name: Dr George Sikalengo
a1002.title: Regional Technical Lead for AIDS, USAID Afya Yangu Southern Project
a1002.speech: Said that they are well organized to ensure that they provide services of HIV for the community and especially the youth ahead of World AIDS Day 2024 ; "The two projects have been supporting the access to quality and offering friendly services of AIDS and tuberculosis to the community in Ruvuma Region. However, as the climax World AIDS Day 2024 comes near, we have organized ourselves very well and increased our efforts to continue providing HIV services to anyone who visits our pavilion" ; "Here we provide testing services as well as connecting those who reveal HIV infections to treatment and care clinics (CTC), continuous treatment services i.e. antiretroviral drugs, collaborative tuberculosis services, testing of cervical cancer, family planning services as well as referrals for services for victims of various types of violence." ; "Similarly, we are providing educational services for behavioral change to the community with the aim of increasing the ability of the community to come to health centers and request services," adding that USAID Afya Yangu Southern has also increased the ability of the community to identify those in need of services and motivate them to join/go to get the relevant service.

a1083.speaker: Management and Development for Health (MDH) letter signed by Chief Executive Officer Dr David Sando
a1083.name: Management and Development for Health (MDH) letter signed by Chief Executive Officer Dr David Sando
a1083.speech: Announced unpaid leave for workers of the integrated health project in Tanzania following a stop-work order. "As explained in earlier communications regarding this cooperative agreement, in accordance with the Executive Order of the President (Donald Trump) on the review and realignment of United States foreign assistance, all activities related to PEPFAR funds were suspended," ; "Including activities carried out under sub-awards and sub-contracts, during the 90-day review period ordered in that order," the letter stated.

a1083.speaker: Management and Development for Health (MDH) letter signed by Chief Executive Officer Dr David Sando
a1083.name: Management and Development for Health (MDH) letter signed by Chief Executive Officer Dr David Sando
a1083.speech: "We ask every project employee to submit a request for voluntary unpaid leave as soon as possible, but not later than the end of today (February 11)." ; "This voluntary unpaid leave will formally begin for a period of 90 days, from February 1 to May 1, 2025, or until we receive further instructions from the donor allowing the project implementation to continue, whichever comes first," the letter said. It clarified and emphasised that this temporary step is not a retrenchment or termination of employment; rather it is a necessary and precautionary measure to manage financial obligations responsibly while MDH awaits the restoration of funding. The letter also notified the relevant authorities, including the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA), the Workers Compensation Fund (WCF), the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF), the Public Service Social Security Fund (PSSSF) and the Higher Education Students' Loans Board (HELSB) about the changes, to avoid any possible penalties arising from non-payment or delayed payments.

a1083.speaker: Management and Development for Health (MDH) letter signed by Chief Executive Officer Dr David Sando
a1083.name: Management and Development for Health (MDH) letter signed by Chief Executive Officer Dr David Sando
a1083.speech: Directed all employees not to speak to the media. "No employee is permitted to speak to the media on behalf of the project head, except with special permission from the Executive Director of MDH." ; "We value your understanding and cooperation during this difficult period. We recognise your commitment to our mission and we are determined to keep you informed at every step as the situation continues to change," the letter stated.

a1083.speaker: Dk Hamad Nyembea, Director of the Curative Services Department, Ministry of Health of Tanzania
a1083.name: Dk Hamad Nyembea
a1083.title: Director of the Curative Services Department, Ministry of Health of Tanzania
a1083.speech: When asked by Mwananchi, said an analysis has already been done on the shortage that will arise and facilities have already made adjustments by looking at alternatives. "If it is a hospital or a health centre, they have already looked at the areas where there will be a shortage and made arrangements for those staff employed by the Government so that they can fill those positions and services are not disrupted," he said. He said the Government does not expect that there will be a problem, services will continue to be provided as usual and it does not expect challenges. "The Government this financial year employed many staff, and two years ago too; this has happened at a time when there are already new hires, these others were adding strength," he said. Asked whether the shortage will bring a burden to the workers who remain at the facilities, Dr Nyembea said: "The burden is there, yes, but the facilities are organising themselves well; places that have more staff have sent them to places with fewer staff, this is an issue that the Government will carry," he said.

a1083.speaker: Ibrahim Hamidu, Head of the Government Communication Unit, Prime Minister's Office (Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons with Disabilities)
a1083.name: Ibrahim Hamidu
a1083.title: Head of the Government Communication Unit, Prime Minister's Office (Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons with Disabilities)
a1083.speech: Asked what the Government is doing to ensure services are not shaken, said: "We are here to ensure that workers' entitlements are handled in accordance with the contracts; the question of what will happen to services is handled by Tamisemi together with the Ministry of Health. MDH we cooperate with them on youth issues; reproductive and health matters are under them."

a1083.speaker: Dk Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a1083.name: Dk Mugisha Nkoronko
a1083.title: President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a1083.speech: Said the directive will shake the health sector because some professionals at health facilities in urban and rural areas depend on salaries from organisations that receive funding from the United States, including MDH. He said that besides workers who work directly in those organisations and civil society organisations, a large proportion are health sector workers employed at public health service facilities whose salaries come from that organisation. He named those who identify patients in the community, community mobilisers for HIV testing and community-level service providers. "There are doctors, nurses employed at several facilities, social welfare, laboratory specialists, project officers who carry out project evaluations, accountants, those dealing with supplies, mid-level medical cadre workers, clinicians and many others," he said. He said almost every cadre in health had the opportunity to work on various projects associated with USAID or PEPFAR.

a1169.speaker: EU Deforestation Regulation (text of the regulation)
a1169.name: EU Deforestation Regulation (text of the regulation)
a1169.speech: The regulation prohibits the entry of commodities linked to deforestation after December 2020, including beef, unless stringent environmental standards are met. The regulation stipulates that products including cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, soy, timber, rubber, and derivatives such as chocolate and furniture must adhere to stringent environmental and social standards.

a1169.speaker: Carl Schlettwein, Namibian Minister of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform
a1169.name: Carl Schlettwein
a1169.title: Namibian Minister of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform
a1169.speech: In his address to the National Assembly, warned that non-compliance could lead to severe penalties: "Non-compliance will result in the following: Fines can reach up to 4% of the operator's or traders's annual EU turnover. Confiscation: Revenues from relevant transactions may be confiscated. Exclusion: Temporary exclusion from public procurement and access to public funding for a maximum of 12 months. Suspension: Temporary suspension from placing or making available on the EU market or exporting relevant commodities/products, along with a prohibition from exercising simplified due diligence."

a1169.speaker: Carl Schlettwein, Namibian Minister of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform
a1169.name: Carl Schlettwein
a1169.title: Namibian Minister of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform
a1169.speech: Acknowledged that while the regulation presents compliance challenges, it also offers Namibia an opportunity to enhance its forest governance and environmental policies. He called for a multi-stakeholder approach, urging various ministries, agencies, and local farmers to collaborate in preparing for the Deforestation Regulation ; "Preparatory steps may include, but are not limited to understanding and analysing the requirements; identifying relevant state actors concerned by the requirements; reviewing the legal framework and existing national and international approaches to guarantee compliance; developing strategies to consolidate and harmonise legal frameworks, especially through participatory approaches; defining indicators for legal compliance; sensitising local farmers about the content of the legislation and how to comply with it; developing legality assurance systems through auditing, certification, and chain of custody requirements; strengthening compliance with the legal framework's standard operating procedures and law enforcement strategies; and supporting independent forest monitoring to verify compliance."

a1362.speaker: South African government
a1362.name: South African government
a1362.speech: "has explained that it enjoys good relations with both Russia and the Ukraine; hence it abstained in the UN General Assembly vote condemning the Russian invasion."

a1362.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1362.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1362.title: President of South Africa
a1362.speech: "subsequently said South Africa abstained because the resolution did not foreground the call for meaningful engagement."

a1362.speaker: Democratic Alliance (official opposition party, South Africa)
a1362.name: Democratic Alliance (official opposition party
a1362.title: South Africa)
a1362.speech: "lost no time in taunting the governing African National Congress (ANC) that its abstention was because a Russian oligarch, Victor Vekselberg, had donated R7.5 million to the ANC."

a1435.speaker: Cobalt Institute
a1435.name: Cobalt Institute
a1435.speech: says demand this year could increase by more than 10% ; says that overall, global demand could reach as much as 227,000 tonnes, 11% more than last year.

a1435.speaker: Kinshasa (Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo)
a1435.name: Kinshasa (Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo)
a1435.speech: hoped its decision would stabilise the market and protect the interests of Congolese producers and investors.

a1444.speaker: United States (government indication)
a1444.name: United States (government indication)
a1444.speech: Already, the US has indicated that it will not be a haven for criminals from other countries who seek refuge there.

a1505.speaker: World leaders, from US President Donald Trump to Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni
a1505.name: World leaders
a1505.title: from US President Donald Trump to Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni
a1505.speech: have appreciated India's timely assistance against a merciless pandemic.

a1505.speaker: Vladimir Norov, Secretary-General of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
a1505.name: Vladimir Norov
a1505.title: Secretary-General of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
a1505.speech: observed that India is playing the role as the pharmacy of the world during the Covid-19 pandemic with its vast experience and deep knowledge in medicine, setting the tone for many regional and global initiatives.

a1505.speaker: Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India
a1505.name: Narendra Modi
a1505.title: Prime Minister of India
a1505.speech: hosted a virtual conference of the leaders of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) and pledged $10 million to a SAARC Emergency Fund to combat the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) in the region. At the first virtual G20 summit, PM Modi underlined the imperative for a new kind of humane globalization, which goes beyond economic and financial calculations. ; India's work in the UNSC will be guided by 5Ss, in Prime Minister Modi's words: Sammaan – Respect; Samwad – Dialogue; Sahyog – Cooperation; Shanti – Peace, to create conditions for universal; and Samriddhi (Prosperity).

a1505.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1505.name: Donald Trump
a1505.title: US President
a1505.speech: has proposed the expansion of the G7 grouping of the world's wealthiest countries to include India, Australia, South Korea and Russia.

a1505.speaker: S. Jaishankar, External Affairs Minister of India
a1505.name: S. Jaishankar
a1505.title: External Affairs Minister of India
a1505.speech: underscored that India "can play a positive global role," in the extraordinary situation spawned by the pandemic and stressed that India seeks to move toward NORMS, a 'New Orientation for a Reformed Multilateral System.' Outlining India's priorities in the UNSC, he said: "We have always been a voice of reason and a votary of international law. We advocate dialogue, consultation and fairness in our approach to global issues. And we emphasize global development, addressing climate change and eradicating of poverty as central to planet's future."

a1533.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1533.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1533.speech: Officially announced the theme of World Health Day 2025, 'Healthy beginnings, hopeful futures', which is expected to focus on improving maternal and newborn health and survival ; says that, according to the most recent estimates, close to 300,000 women lose their life due to pregnancy or childbirth each year, over two million babies die in their first month of life and around two million more are stillborn: "This is roughly one preventable death every seven seconds – losses which bring tremendous sadness and heartache to millions of families around the world" ; adds that, while maternal and newborn deaths occur in all regions, the vast majority are in the poorest countries and those facing conflict and other crises ; further states that based on current trends, four out of five countries are off track to meet the United Nations' global targets for improving maternal survival by 2030 and that one in three will fail to meet targets for reducing newborn deaths.

a1533.speaker: Anshu Banerjee, Director of Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health and Ageing at WHO
a1533.name: Anshu Banerjee
a1533.title: Director of Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health and Ageing at WHO
a1533.speech: "The focus of this campaign comes at a crucial moment, aiming to help countries regain lost progress while showcasing new research and evidence that will enhance the health of women and babies globally" ; added that "as rollbacks to humanitarian assistance jeopardise a critical lifeline for millions, it will also be an opportunity to step up support and collaboration for global health – and deliver hope to those in urgent need of lifesaving care."

a1533.speaker: Pascale Allotey, Director for Sexual and Reproductive Health and Research at WHO
a1533.name: Pascale Allotey
a1533.title: Director for Sexual and Reproductive Health and Research at WHO
a1533.speech: Said it is not sufficient that women survive childbirth but they must also be able to enjoy their lives in good health: "Women and girls everywhere need access to health providers who listen to their concerns and meet their needs, while ensuring they can plan their fertility, take charge of their futures and protect their health."

a1533.speaker: Malawi Health Sector Strategic Plan III 2023–2030 (report)
a1533.name: Malawi Health Sector Strategic Plan III 2023–2030 (report)
a1533.speech: Reported that maternal mortality fell from 439 deaths per 100,000 live births to 349 in 2019.

a1533.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a1533.name: Experts (unnamed)
a1533.speech: Say more remains to be done, as efforts to improve maternal, newborn and child health are thwarted by several factors including gaps in health system financing.

a1629.speaker: Police investigation (Liberia National Police)
a1629.name: Police investigation (Liberia National Police)
a1629.speech: During police investigation, it was established that suspect Bill Sonkarlay engaged in an altercation with the deceased at her mother's place, carrying with him a stick that he did not use; the suspect has been charged with manslaughter, a violation of Chapter 14, Section 14.2 of the Revised Penal Law of Liberia.

a1629.speaker: Eyewitnesses
a1629.name: Eyewitnesses
a1629.speech: Told police investigators that the suspect went to complain to the deceased's mother, Marthaline Paye, concerning the attitude of her daughter towards him and his girlfriend, accusing him of being a drug user, which angered him.

a1629.speaker: Marthaline Paye, mother of the deceased
a1629.name: Marthaline Paye
a1629.title: mother of the deceased
a1629.speech: After failing to calm her daughter, the mother backed off, stating that her daughter was a grown-up woman who never took advice, and they should continue with whatever they were doing.

a1629.speaker: Neighbors of the victim
a1629.name: Neighbors of the victim
a1629.speech: According to them, the victim had a sickle cell problem.

a1629.speaker: Judge Blamo Dixon, Criminal Court 'C'
a1629.name: Judge Blamo Dixon
a1629.title: Criminal Court 'C'
a1629.speech: In his ruling on January 28, 2025, said: "Evidence adduced in court by prosecuting lawyers, was convincing to convict defendant George Obi for having drugs"; his decision acquitted four other defendants who were indicted along with 'Japan' on grounds that pieces of evidence were insufficient to link them to the crime.

a1629.speaker: Lawyer for the convicted defendants
a1629.name: Lawyer for the convicted defendants
a1629.speech: Took an exception to Judge Dixon's verdict, awaiting his final judgment before announcing an appeal to the Supreme Court to overturn the lower court's decision.

a1632.speaker: US Supreme Court (ruling)
a1632.name: US Supreme Court (ruling)
a1632.speech: Has authorized the White House to deport immigrants to third countries, including conflict-stricken South Sudan and Libya, regardless of where the individuals are originally from. The decision handed down on Monday lifts an earlier order by a lower court that had blocked the emergency removals due to safety concerns.

a1632.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1632.name: Donald Trump
a1632.title: US President
a1632.speech: Has revived a series of hardline immigration measures since returning to office in January, following campaign promises to reverse what he called the "open border" policies of his predecessor, Joe Biden.

a1632.speaker: Brian Murphy, US District Judge
a1632.name: Brian Murphy
a1632.title: US District Judge
a1632.speech: On April 18, ruled that deporting immigrants to nations other than their home countries without due process "unquestionably" violated constitutional protections.

a1632.speaker: Sonia Sotomayor, US Supreme Court Justice (dissenting)
a1632.name: Sonia Sotomayor
a1632.title: US Supreme Court Justice (dissenting)
a1632.speech: Accused Washington of violating the lower court's preliminary injunction. "The government removed six class members to South Sudan with less than 16 hours' notice and no opportunity to be heard," she stated ; Justice Sotomayor said her Supreme Court colleagues should have left the lower courts to handle the "high-stakes litigation with the care" it required, instead of granting "the government emergency relief from an order it has repeatedly defied."

a1632.speaker: US State Department
a1632.name: US State Department
a1632.speech: Has placed both Libya and South Sudan under its highest-level travel advisory, warning Americans not to visit due to armed conflict, crime, and political unrest.

a1632.speaker: US Embassy in South Sudan
a1632.name: US Embassy in South Sudan
a1632.speech: In March, withdrew non-emergency personnel, citing deteriorating security conditions.

a1652.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1652.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1652.title: President of Ghana
a1652.speech: lauded the outgoing British High Commissioner for her "positive engagements" throughout her time in the country, and reflected on the long-standing historical relationship between Ghana and the UK, describing it as having been "so far so good" ; emphasised the mutual need for deeper economic partnerships and trade moving forward, and noted the dynamic changes in the global landscape, including the diminishing nature of traditional development assistance and the necessity for developing countries like Ghana to strategically reposition themselves.

a1652.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1652.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1652.title: President of Ghana
a1652.speech: acknowledged the UK's significant support in counter-terrorism efforts, specifically commending cooperation in intelligence gathering and training: "We appreciate the partnership we have shared in the fight against terrorism. We will continue to rely on the UK for help and cooperation in intelligence gathering and training to prepare ourselves in the event of any attack."

a1652.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1652.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1652.title: President of Ghana
a1652.speech: updated the High Commissioner on his recent proactive engagements with leaders in the Sahelian countries, including Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, and pledged further diplomatic efforts aimed at rebuilding trust and improving relationships with these neighbours ; announced that the upcoming ECOWAS meeting on Sunday would place the issues concerning the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) at the top of its agenda: "I am going to have the opportunity to report to the rest of the ECOWAS leaders on trips I made to the three countries and share some of my perspectives about their grievances and how we can redefine relationships."

a1652.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1652.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1652.title: President of Ghana
a1652.speech: provided an optimistic outlook on the domestic economy, reporting progress with a strengthening Cedi, declining inflation, and renewed investor confidence: "I am happy to report that it's going well. The first quarter report on economic performance indicates a GDP growth of 5.3 per cent, inflation has reduced from 23 per cent to 18 per cent since January, and we hope to bring it down to 13 per cent by the end of the year, so that should create some relief for Ghanaians in terms of the cost of living and we will continue to maintain fiscal discipline."

a1652.speaker: Harriet Thompson, outgoing British High Commissioner to Ghana
a1652.name: Harriet Thompson
a1652.title: outgoing British High Commissioner to Ghana
a1652.speech: expressed her gratitude for the warm support and cooperation she received during her tenure and acknowledged the successful implementation of various British-sponsored interventions during her time.

a1676.speaker: Mmamoloko Kubayi, South African Justice Minister and Inter-Ministerial Committee chairperson
a1676.name: Mmamoloko Kubayi
a1676.title: South African Justice Minister and Inter-Ministerial Committee chairperson
a1676.speech: Made the assurance at a recent media briefing in Johannesburg that the South African government is continuing its work in facilitating the safe return of foreign nationals to their respective home countries.

a1676.speaker: Malawian nationals gathered outside Malawi's Consulate General in Johannesburg
a1676.name: Malawian nationals gathered outside Malawi's Consulate General in Johannesburg
a1676.speech: Saying they feared for their safety as a June 30 ultimatum from anti-migrant groups drew closer.

a1676.speaker: Commissioner Reinhard !Haoseb, Namibia's Police attache at the Namibian High Commission in Pretoria, South Africa
a1676.name: Commissioner Reinhard !Haoseb
a1676.title: Namibia's Police attache at the Namibian High Commission in Pretoria, South Africa
a1676.speech: Confirmed that a Namibian truck driver, Vilho Njati, who was reported missing in South Africa, was found last night.

a1676.speaker: Some political party representatives who accompanied the Electoral Commission of Namibia (ECN) to Johannesburg to observe the printing of ballot papers
a1676.name: Some political party representatives who accompanied the Electoral Commission of Namibia (ECN) to Johannesburg to observe the printing of ballot papers
a1676.speech: Have voiced concerns over the transparency of the process.

a1676.speaker: Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation (Namibia)
a1676.name: Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation (Namibia)
a1676.speech: Has expressed concern at the unfortunate incident during which a Namibian national lost his eyesight in Johannesburg, South Africa, last week.

a1724.speaker: Fatima Ali, community mobiliser working with UNFPA in Maiduguri, Borno State
a1724.name: Fatima Ali
a1724.title: community mobiliser working with UNFPA in Maiduguri, Borno State
a1724.speech: "The water came up to our chests" ; "We kept walking for two hours on flooded roads" ; "It happened two weeks before my due date. As I am pregnant, I could not walk alone. It was my husband who helped me cross the water" ; "even with the floods, I keep working. The reason is that I want to encourage other women" ; "In UNFPA's work, we prioritise maternal health above all... And when I give birth, I will be even more passionate about helping women, having experienced first-hand what motherhood is."

a1724.speaker: Mustapha Hussein, digital literacy facilitator with UNFPA in Maiduguri
a1724.name: Mustapha Hussein
a1724.title: digital literacy facilitator with UNFPA in Maiduguri
a1724.speech: "As a humanitarian worker, it is not easy to provide assistance to the affected population when you are affected yourself" ; "Almost our entire community was submerged by the floods" ; "Walking 7 km from here to the camp was not easy. And then it was also terrible and frightening" ; "I am recovering now and bouncing back" ; "My next step is to start rebuilding my house from scratch" ; "As a humanitarian worker and someone who grew up in a complex emergency situation, this flood has not held me back."

a1724.speaker: UNFPA report circulated by the APO group on behalf of UNFPA
a1724.name: UNFPA report circulated by the APO group on behalf of UNFPA
a1724.speech: According to the report, more than 14,000 displaced people have received information on sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and more than 1,500 dignity kits containing essential hygiene products, including sanitary pads, underwear and soap, have been distributed in flood-affected areas.

a1724.speaker: Data on flood-affected countries (cited)
a1724.name: Data on flood-affected countries (cited)
a1724.speech: Data show an increased risk of early and forced marriage and of intimate partner violence in flood-affected countries such as Cameroon.

a1744.speaker: Sports source (anonymous), cited by AMAP
a1744.name: Sports source (anonymous)
a1744.title: cited by AMAP
a1744.speech: AMAP learned from a sports source that the Malian Football Federation (Femafoot), after a series of postponements, has set the start of the national football championship for 23 November for the 2024-2025 season.

a1813.speaker: Joakim Reiter, Vodafone Foundation chief external and corporate affairs officer
a1813.name: Joakim Reiter
a1813.title: Vodafone Foundation chief external and corporate affairs officer
a1813.speech: Expressed excitement about the expansion, saying, "The M-Mama Initiative is a lifeline for rural communities. It's a solution that has worked in other countries, and we are confident it will save many lives here in Malawi."

a1813.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a1813.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a1813.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a1813.speech: Welcomed the initiative, emphasizing the need for innovative approaches to tackling maternal mortality. "This is a crucial project that will make a real difference in saving the lives of women and children, particularly in our rural areas. The government is fully committed to supporting it."

a1813.speaker: Dr. Mary Phiri, maternal health specialist in Lilongwe
a1813.name: Dr. Mary Phiri
a1813.title: maternal health specialist in Lilongwe
a1813.speech: Is optimistic about the impact the service will have on rural communities. "We have lost too many women simply because they couldn't get to a health facility in time. This service will be a game-changer."

a1961.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a1961.name: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a1961.speech: According to the FAO, the materials donated are through its Emergency Centre for Trans-boundary Animal Diseases (ECTAD) program as part of efforts to combat zoonosis in Liberia.

a1961.speaker: Dr. Ibrahim Amed, FAO Country Representative and Head of the ECTAD Program
a1961.name: Dr. Ibrahim Amed
a1961.title: FAO Country Representative and Head of the ECTAD Program
a1961.speech: Said the gesture will assist Community Animal Health Workers to strengthen surveillance across the country.

a1961.speaker: Jim Wright, USAID Mission Director
a1961.name: Jim Wright
a1961.title: USAID Mission Director
a1961.speech: Said the motorbikes will help Community Animal Health Workers expand their reach and respond to diseases more effectively.

a1961.speaker: Fotton Blasin, Assistant Agriculture Minister for Administration, Liberia
a1961.name: Fotton Blasin
a1961.title: Assistant Agriculture Minister for Administration, Liberia
a1961.speech: Hailed the FAO and USAID for empowering the animal health sector to tackle zoonosis ; indicated that this does not only represent motorbikes but also symbolizes hope and progress in the sector ; added that the donation will have a trickle down effect on the health of the population: “the Ministry will still again knock to their doors for additional support.”

a1987.speaker: Col. Suleiman Ibrahim, ATMIS military Chief Engineer (representing ATMIS Force Headquarters)
a1987.name: Col. Suleiman Ibrahim
a1987.title: ATMIS military Chief Engineer (representing ATMIS Force Headquarters)
a1987.speech: "This significant event demonstrates the growing capacity and dedication of the Somali Security Forces to take over the security reponsibilities of Somalia, with the support of ATMIS, UNSOS and other partners" ; commended ATMIS and SNAF troops for jointly pacifying the Lower Juba region, paving way for the Somali-led transition process ; "I commend the Somali Security Forces for their display of character in holding on to all the military bases handed over… I am confident that in partnership with all of us, they will continue to exhibit their capabilities and ensure the return of lasting peace to Somalia."

a1987.speaker: Gen. Mohamed Ibrahim Farah, Badhadhe District Commissioner
a1987.name: Gen. Mohamed Ibrahim Farah
a1987.title: Badhadhe District Commissioner
a1987.speech: Said the Federal Government of Somalia is ready to defend its territory and the people against Al-Shabaab: "It is now time for Somalis to take charge of their own security. We are ready to take over this base and continue to maintain its security. Somalia now has a strong government that can take charge of its security."

a1987.speaker: Col. Meshack Kishoyian, ATMIS Sector Two Commander
a1987.name: Col. Meshack Kishoyian
a1987.title: ATMIS Sector Two Commander
a1987.speech: "This FOB has been very key in curtailing Al-Shabaab activities within this region. Being a port town, it has managed to block imports of unwanted items into this region."

a1987.speaker: Maj. Sakariye Mohamed Omar, SNAF representative
a1987.name: Maj. Sakariye Mohamed Omar
a1987.title: SNAF representative
a1987.speech: Acknowledged the ATMIS KDF troops' contributions in degrading Al-Shabaab: "Somalia has now become much safer, and the momentum of our forces remains undeterred."

a1999.speaker: The White House
a1999.name: The White House
a1999.speech: Announced the implementation of a large-scale deportation operation, following Donald Trump’s inauguration for his second term.

a1999.speaker: Karoline Leavitt, White House spokesperson
a1999.name: Karoline Leavitt
a1999.title: White House spokesperson
a1999.speech: Said 538 migrants in an irregular situation had been arrested and several hundred of them expelled from the country by military aircraft, describing the arrests as “criminal illegal immigration” and saying they include individuals deemed particularly dangerous, such as a suspected terrorist, members of the Tren de Aragua gang, and several people convicted of sexual crimes against minors; “Promises made, promises kept,” Leavitt affirmed.

a1999.speaker: Tom Homan, former director of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), to Fox News
a1999.name: Tom Homan
a1999.title: former director of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), to Fox News
a1999.speech: Had predicted mass arrests across the country: “Chicago is only one place among others,” insisting that the operation would affect many American cities.

a1999.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a1999.name: Donald Trump
a1999.title: President of the United States
a1999.speech: Had made illegal immigration a priority during his presidential campaign, promising strong action against undocumented migrants, and insisted on the deportation of “criminal aliens”.

a1999.speaker: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) data
a1999.name: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) data
a1999.speech: According to ICE, nearly 425,000 of the roughly 12 million undocumented migrants in the United States have a criminal record, including 13,000 for homicide.

a1999.speaker: Ras J. Baraka, Mayor of Newark
a1999.name: Ras J. Baraka
a1999.title: Mayor of Newark
a1999.speech: Denounced raids by immigration agents who carried out arrests, including of American citizens, without presenting a legal warrant.

a2026.speaker: David Layton, Genesee County Prosecutor
a2026.name: David Layton
a2026.title: Genesee County Prosecutor
a2026.speech: Told the media on Monday that Sharmel had argued with and spat at the security guard before driving off; she returned later with her son, and reportedly it was the son who fired the gun.

a2026.speaker: David Layton, Genesee County Prosecutor
a2026.name: David Layton
a2026.title: Genesee County Prosecutor
a2026.speech: Told journalists: "The death of Calvin Munerlyn is senseless and tragic, and those who did it must be brought to account as required by law."

a2026.speaker: Gretchen Whitmer, Governor of Michigan
a2026.name: Gretchen Whitmer
a2026.title: Governor of Michigan
a2026.speech: Told all residents to wear masks when they are inside businesses in order to fight Covid-19; stores may refuse to provide service to anyone who does not comply with this rule.

a2026.speaker: BBC
a2026.name: BBC
a2026.speech: Cited as the source of the report, including that as of Monday the number of people infected in Michigan stood at 43,950, including 4,135 deaths.

a2210.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a2210.name: Marco Rubio
a2210.title: US Secretary of State
a2210.speech: Ordered USAID's incorporation into the State Department as of Tuesday.

a2210.speaker: Barack Obama, former US President
a2210.name: Barack Obama
a2210.title: former US President
a2210.speech: Described the dismantling of USAID by the administration led by Republican Donald Trump as "a colossal mistake".

a2210.speaker: George W. Bush, former US President
a2210.name: George W. Bush
a2210.title: former US President
a2210.speech: Speaking in a recorded message, went directly to the cuts to a landmark AIDS and HIV programme launched by his Republican government and credited with saving 25 million lives around the world.

a2210.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2210.name: Donald Trump
a2210.title: US President
a2210.speech: Claimed the agency was run by "radical left lunatics" and infested with "tremendous fraud".

a2210.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire and Trump ally
a2210.name: Elon Musk
a2210.title: billionaire and Trump ally

a2210.speaker: Bono, musician, leader of the band U2 and humanitarian activist
a2210.name: Bono
a2210.title: musician, leader of the band U2 and humanitarian activist
a2210.speech: Announced as the "surprise guest", held back tears at some moments as he recited a poem he had written for the agency and its devastation; spoke about children dying of malnutrition.

a2210.speaker: Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf, former President of Liberia; Juan Manuel Santos, former President of Colombia; and Linda Thomas-Greenfield, former US Ambassador to the UN
a2210.name: Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf
a2210.title: former President of Liberia; Juan Manuel Santos, former President of Colombia; and Linda Thomas-Greenfield, former US Ambassador to the UN
a2210.speech: Also spoke to the USAID officials and staff during the videoconference.

a2210.speaker: Officials and leaders at the USAID farewell videoconference
a2210.name: Officials and leaders at the USAID farewell videoconference
a2210.speech: Expressed their appreciation for the thousands of USAID employees who lost their jobs and their life's work, in comments that were at times furious and often tearful.

a2210.speaker: Researchers at Boston University and other analysts
a2210.name: Researchers at Boston University and other analysts
a2210.speech: Say millions of people will die because of the US cuts to funding for health and other programmes abroad.

a2210.speaker: US State Department
a2210.name: US State Department
a2210.speech: Said it will present this week USAID's successor programme for foreign assistance, which will be called "America First". "The new process will ensure proper oversight and that every taxpayer dollar spent will help advance our national interests," the US diplomatic service stressed.

a2293.speaker: Edwin Dikoloti, Minister of Health and Wellness (Botswana)
a2293.name: Edwin Dikoloti
a2293.title: Minister of Health and Wellness (Botswana)
a2293.speech: Botswana is expecting 1.15 million doses after paying US$7 million into the African Union arrangement in April, according to Health and Wellness minister, Edwin Dikoloti. Briefing Parliament last week, Dikoloti said government was expecting the doses between August and September.

a2293.speaker: African Union (statement)
a2293.name: African Union (statement)
a2293.speech: According to an African Union statement this afternoon, part of the 400 million doses will be manufactured in South Africa, where Johnson & Johnson recently signed a fill-finish deal with Gqeberha (formerly Port Elizabeth)-based pharmaceutical firm, Aspen.

a2307.speaker: Ibrahim Matola, Malawi Minister of Energy (Ministry of Energy letter dated February 11, 2025)
a2307.name: Ibrahim Matola
a2307.title: Malawi Minister of Energy (Ministry of Energy letter dated February 11, 2025)
a2307.speech: "I, Ibrahim Matola, Minister of Energy, by virtue of the powers vested in me by Section 6A(2) of the Liquid Fuels and Gas (Production and Supply) Amendment Act, 2025, do hereby nominate the National Oil Company of Malawi as a government agent responsible for the importation of diesel and petrol into the country through Government-to-Government fuel supply arrangement," reads the letter ; The document further states that the deal aims to alleviate the ongoing fuel crisis and provide Malawi with enough time to finalize direct importation agreements with Gulf oil-producing countries.

a2307.speaker: Alfonso Chikuni, Principal Secretary for Energy
a2307.name: Alfonso Chikuni
a2307.title: Principal Secretary for Energy
a2307.speech: When contacted for comment, referred inquiries to the Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (MERA): "MERA might be in a position to comment because I might not be aware of these new developments," Chikuni said.

a2307.speaker: Raymond Likambale, Nocma spokesperson
a2307.name: Raymond Likambale
a2307.title: Nocma spokesperson
a2307.speech: confirmed the company’s role as the government’s agent but declined to provide further details: "The ministry is the policyholder. Allow us to refer you to the Ministry of Energy," he said.

a2307.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Government spokesperson, and Austin Theu, Ministry of Energy spokesperson
a2307.name: Moses Kunkuyu
a2307.title: Government spokesperson, and Austin Theu, Ministry of Energy spokesperson
a2307.speech: also requested additional time before responding to inquiries on the matter.

a2462.speaker: Simplex Chithyola-Banda, Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a2462.name: Simplex Chithyola-Banda
a2462.title: Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a2462.speech: Says Malawi has made significant strides in aligning with the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) Programme of Action to accelerate sustainable economic development ; He said Malawi's commitment towards the ICDP programme of action implementation remains a priority ; "For instance, life expectancy in Malawi has jumped from 62 years to 65 years within the past few years with the fertility rate declining to 3.7 from 4.4 children per woman. Use of contraceptives moved from 58 percent to 66 percent with the maternal mortality rate dropping from 439 to 381 per 100 000 live births."

a2462.speaker: Simplex Chithyola-Banda, Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a2462.name: Simplex Chithyola-Banda
a2462.title: Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a2462.speech: The minister said the worrisome challenge was non-communicable diseases which contribute to 40 percent of deaths in Malawi ; Chithyola-Banda said government was providing integrated health services through construction of 900 health posts.

a2462.speaker: Shelton Kanyanda, National Statistical Office commissioner (Malawi)
a2462.name: Shelton Kanyanda
a2462.title: National Statistical Office commissioner (Malawi)
a2462.speech: Said building and strengthening stronger partnerships with the United Nations (UN) agencies on healthcare systems and resilience would greatly benefit Malawi ; "Malawi is mobilising domestic and external resources through the Integrated National Financing Framework and also impeded climate resilience and emergency preparedness into the health policies."

a2496.speaker: Official data (Statistics South Africa)
a2496.name: Official data (Statistics South Africa)
a2496.speech: Showed on Tuesday that South Africa's unemployment rate rose for the second quarter in a row, standing at 33.2% in April-June, up from 32.9% in January-March.

a2496.speaker: Statistics South Africa
a2496.name: Statistics South Africa
a2496.speech: Said the number of unemployed people increased to 8.367 million in the second quarter, though there was a slight drop in an expanded definition of unemployment, which includes those discouraged from seeking work; six of the 10 industries tracked by the agency recorded employment decreases, while four had increases.

a2496.speaker: Risenga Maluleke, top statistics official
a2496.name: Risenga Maluleke
a2496.title: top statistics official
a2496.speech: Said it was too early to tell whether U.S. tariffs were having an effect on the jobs data.

a2496.speaker: Risenga Maluleke, top statistics official
a2496.name: Risenga Maluleke
a2496.title: top statistics official
a2496.speech: Dismissed criticism by the former head of major local bank Capitec that the statistics agency was underestimating the number of people with informal jobs; he told a press conference his agency had always measured that and made its numbers available, adding that South Africa would be making "a big mistake as a country if we want to assume that we do not have an unemployment challenge".

a2496.speaker: Former head of Capitec bank
a2496.name: Former head of Capitec bank
a2496.speech: Criticised the statistics agency for underestimating the number of people with informal jobs.

a2496.speaker: Desiree Manamela, chief director of labour statistics
a2496.name: Desiree Manamela
a2496.title: chief director of labour statistics
a2496.speech: Said updates to the way Statistics SA collects unemployment data that will be rolled out in the next quarter were unlikely to significantly affect the official jobless rate, but they should allow the agency to include additional measures of the health of the economy in its reports.

a2574.speaker: Judge Hilary Squires
a2574.name: Judge Hilary Squires
a2574.speech: “Shaik’s payments to Zuma were an investment in political influence.”

a2574.speaker: Judge Kate O’Regan, writing for a unanimous Constitutional Court
a2574.name: Judge Kate O’Regan
a2574.title: writing for a unanimous Constitutional Court
a2574.speech: “There can be no doubt the money received by Shaik from his businesses were the proceeds of a bribe.”

a2574.speaker: Constitution of South Africa, section 84(2)(j)
