a2574.name: Constitution of South Africa
a2574.title: section 84(2)(j)
a2574.speech: Says the President is responsible for “pardoning or reprieving offenders and remitting any fines, penalties or forfeitures.”

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: Says he is now matured and ready to govern Malawi with insightful leadership; in an exclusive interview with Zodiak Television he confirmed his intention to be on the ballot in 2025, emphasizing that Malawians will vote for him to lead the country as President.

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: On priority areas for development: key focus areas include food security, energy, export promotion, education reform, tourism revitalization, and healthcare, with a strong emphasis on ensuring Malawi becomes food secure.

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: On economic independence: emphasized that Malawi has enough resources to generate wealth, advocating for innovative thinking and establishing a Sovereign Wealth Fund to reduce reliance on foreign aid.

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: On reforming governance: proposed a new leadership style where the President is seen as a servant, not a boss, encouraging citizens to address him as "Mr. President" instead of "His Excellency."

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: On political strategy and alliances: the UDF is not considering alliances at the moment, intending to independently contest and serve Malawians; Muluzi reflected on past alliances as limiting voter choice.

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: On the Thangata system and farmer empowerment: criticized the exploitative system where poor farmers are disadvantaged, and promised to end this cycle and introduce policies to protect and empower smallholder farmers.

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: On elections and democratic processes: dismissed criticism of his uncontested candidacy within the UDF, comparing it to global examples like Donald Trump's nomination in the Republican Party, asserting it reflects the will of the people.

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: On changing voter mentality: encouraged Malawians to vote based on hope and a vision for better governance rather than anger or frustration.

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: On learning from the past: acknowledged the lessons from UDF's loss in 2020 and his own temporary resignation, stating that he used the time to travel, learn, and return with renewed insights to serve Malawi.

a2699.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2699.title: leader of the opposition United Democratic Front (UDF)
a2699.speech: On generational leadership: while recognizing his family's political legacy, emphasized his independence and the importance of learning from past leaders while addressing contemporary challenges.

a2763.speaker: Christopher Sankolo, Director-General of the Liberia Agriculture Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA)
a2763.name: Christopher Sankolo
a2763.title: Director-General of the Liberia Agriculture Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA)
a2763.speech: Stated that the retreat is crucial in addressing these challenges and rebranding the institution for better performance, and emphasised the need for partnerships and collaboration with stakeholders to achieve the organization's goals.

a2763.speaker: Moses Gbanyan, Deputy Minister for Extension Services, proxy for the Minister of Agriculture of Liberia
a2763.name: Moses Gbanyan
a2763.title: Deputy Minister for Extension Services, proxy for the Minister of Agriculture of Liberia
a2763.speech: Encouraged participants to actively engage in the discussions and contribute to the development of a strategic plan that will ensure the success of LACRA; also stressed the importance of the agricultural sector in Liberia's economic development and the need for a strong regulatory body to promote and regulate it.

a3060.speaker: Amb. Deike Potzel, Director General for Crisis Prevention, Stabilization, Peacebuilding, and Humanitarian Assistance at the German Federal Foreign Office
a3060.name: Amb. Deike Potzel
a3060.title: Director General for Crisis Prevention, Stabilization, Peacebuilding, and Humanitarian Assistance at the German Federal Foreign Office
a3060.speech: Said despite other pressing global crises, Berlin has maintained its support to South Sudan's fight against hunger, conflict and disasters like floods and droughts, as well as assistance to people fleeing Sudan ; "Germany supports the people of South Sudan as the second largest bilateral donor to counter the huge humanitarian challenges. We have provided more than 60 million Euros last year in humanitarian assistance and will remain engaged this year."

a3060.speaker: German Federal Foreign Office (press statement)
a3060.name: German Federal Foreign Office (press statement)
a3060.speech: "Director General Potzel commended South Sudan's hospitality for refugees from Sudan despite of own hardships."

a3060.speaker: Amb. Deike Potzel, Director General at the German Federal Foreign Office
a3060.name: Amb. Deike Potzel
a3060.title: Director General at the German Federal Foreign Office
a3060.speech: In her engagements with the vice presidents, stressed the urgency to fully and swiftly implement the 2018 peace agreement through constructive dialogue amongst all partners.

a3060.speaker: Amb. Deike Potzel, Director General at the German Federal Foreign Office
a3060.name: Amb. Deike Potzel
a3060.title: Director General at the German Federal Foreign Office
a3060.speech: Underlined that her country's assistance can only complement the sovereign responsibility of the transitional government of South Sudan and not replace it ; "The Transitional Government remains in the driving seat especially when it comes to using the country's resources for humanitarian aid and for the development of the country. Improving transparency on the revenues of natural resources is crucial."

a3096.speaker: Matšeliso Nthunya, 20-year-old pregnant woman at Nazareth Health Centre
a3096.name: Matšeliso Nthunya
a3096.title: 20-year-old pregnant woman at Nazareth Health Centre
a3096.speech: "I would ask Trump how he feels knowing HIV is so dangerous, especially when he's in a position to help people, particularly a small country like Lesotho. I am scared for people living with HIV, because in the end, they will die if they don't take their ARVs." ; "Does he realise how many lives are now at risk because he chose not to help us for his own reasons?" ; "I don't think Trump made the right decision, because many people are going to die. If he wanted to make cuts, he should have done it elsewhere, not here."

a3096.speaker: Matšeliso Nthunya, 20-year-old pregnant woman at Nazareth Health Centre
a3096.name: Matšeliso Nthunya
a3096.title: 20-year-old pregnant woman at Nazareth Health Centre
a3096.speech: "I am HIV-negative, and even my sibling born in 2016 is HIV-negative" ; says her mother's experience has shaped her understanding of what it means to care for herself and her unborn child ; "I must take care of myself because I have seen from my mother that even if a parent is HIV-positive, a child born from that mother can be HIV-negative" ; "I would say a lot of things. I would thank her for taking care of me, for the love she had for me to protect me from being infected at birth… I would say a lot of things – and cry."

a3096.speaker: Mphonyane Thetso, midwife at Nazareth Health Centre
a3096.name: Mphonyane Thetso
a3096.title: midwife at Nazareth Health Centre
a3096.speech: Urges the expectant mothers to deliver their babies at the centre or St Joseph's Hospital in Roma, where, she says, mothers and their babies have a fighting chance not to contract HIV should complications arise ; "Everything is dramatic here" ; "We have records showing that some women delivered their babies in April and May 2025 with invalid (inconclusive) HIV status because they were not retested after we lost our HIV counsellor" ; "Sometimes a pregnant woman tests HIV-negative at her first visit. Then, when she comes back at 36 weeks for a re-test, she tests HIV-positive. A woman can give birth HIV-positive without knowing it if she wasn't retested. But if she tests positive, we can still prevent mother-to-child transmission with ART and PrEP. You can't give PrEP to someone if you don't know their HIV status."

a3096.speaker: Lesotho Ministry of Health (figures)
a3096.name: Lesotho Ministry of Health (figures)
a3096.speech: According to Lesotho's ministry of health, at M1.3 billion a year, PEPFAR accounted for 66.5 percent of the M1.9 billion budget for 2024/25.

a3096.speaker: World Health Organization, August 2023 Disease Outlook report
a3096.name: World Health Organization
a3096.title: August 2023 Disease Outlook report
a3096.speech: According to the report, Lesotho has the world's second-highest HIV prevalence.

a3096.speaker: Dr Tapiwa Tarumbiswa, HIV/Aids Manager, Lesotho Ministry of Health
a3096.name: Dr Tapiwa Tarumbiswa
a3096.title: HIV/Aids Manager, Lesotho Ministry of Health
a3096.speech: Told parliament on May 20 that "HIV-unsuppressed mothers are more likely to infect their children during pregnancy, birth, and breastfeeding" ; "Delayed HIV testing and diagnosis will result (in) increased AIDS-related mortality due to individuals presenting late with advanced HIV disease" ; warns: "The impact of cutting treatment and care services is that, if we are not providing quality treatment and care, there's the potential for an increase in Aids-related deaths."

a3096.speaker: 'Maneo Ntene, Principal Secretary, Lesotho Ministry of Health
a3096.name: 'Maneo Ntene
a3096.title: Principal Secretary, Lesotho Ministry of Health
a3096.speech: Said in an interview on July 8 that the government was not yet in a position to publicly discuss efforts underway to address this funding shortfall ; "We are still working on the modalities of closing that gap. The Ministry of Health is not working alone on this; as we speak, I am driving to the Ministry of Public Service for discussions related to this issue."

a3096.speaker: Dr Tlohang Letsie, senior lecturer at the National University of Lesotho
a3096.name: Dr Tlohang Letsie
a3096.title: senior lecturer at the National University of Lesotho
a3096.speech: Warns that there is little hope of the "American fund to Lesotho" being restored, at least in the near future, because Lesotho lacks minerals that the US can benefit directly from; indicated that the current US administration is motivated by a cost-benefit analysis, referencing countries like DRC and Rwanda ; "Another factor is that Lesotho seems to be hopeless in engaging the US. The country is simply not doing enough. It appears we are waiting for the divine intervention to blow some spirit of philanthropy into the Americans."

a3096.speaker: Dr Tlohang Letsie, senior lecturer at the National University of Lesotho
a3096.name: Dr Tlohang Letsie
a3096.title: senior lecturer at the National University of Lesotho
a3096.speech: Believes China could step in to help fill the funding gap left by the US cuts ; "China has over the years appeared to be an alternative to the West in many regards. It can easily be persuaded to close the gap left by the Americans" ; "We have seen during the Covid-19 era that it can play that role. However, it would take some time to shift from the US strategies to the new Chinese strategies."

a3096.speaker: Mokhothu Makhalanyane, Chairperson of the Social Cluster Portfolio Committee in Lesotho
a3096.name: Mokhothu Makhalanyane
a3096.title: Chairperson of the Social Cluster Portfolio Committee in Lesotho
a3096.speech: Said in a separate interview on July 8: "The Ministry of Health has quantified the actual cost of human and medical resources. The total impact is about M800 million, but we anticipate that this year the cost will be around M250 million. As a result, parliament approved a contingency allocation of about M300 million for health to help address the impact of the US aid cuts."

a3096.speaker: Mokhothu Makhalanyane, Health Committee Chair and head of the Network of African Parliamentary Committees on Health (NEAPACOH)
a3096.name: Mokhothu Makhalanyane
a3096.title: Health Committee Chair and head of the Network of African Parliamentary Committees on Health (NEAPACOH)
a3096.speech: Said most African countries, including Lesotho, are exploring inward funding strategies ; "At a NEAPACOH meeting earlier, no one was talking about how to negotiate with America. People were discussing how to utilise the resources we already have, how to avoid and eliminate waste, and how to increase domestic funding for health" ; added that Lesotho's Ministry of Health is preparing to table a health insurance strategy before Parliament, which once approved and legalised would reduce the government's burden in subsidising health services, noting that countries like South Africa, Zambia, Kenya, Tanzania, and Rwanda have adopted similar models.

a3096.speaker: Mpolokeng Mohloai, Country Director for mothers2mothers Lesotho
a3096.name: Mpolokeng Mohloai
a3096.title: Country Director for mothers2mothers Lesotho
a3096.speech: Said in a June 20 interview with Uncensored News: "HIV transmission rates from mothers to their babies were alarmingly high – in some places as high as 40 percent – largely due to limited access to information, testing, and treatment"; explained that many women only learnt they were HIV-positive late in pregnancy, or not at all, missing crucial windows for intervention ; "The introduction of the Mentor Mothers programme was a game-changer. Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) rates dropped dramatically in the communities where m2m worked." ; "In 2023, we achieved virtual elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV among our enrolled clients for the 10th consecutive year, reaching a 0 percent transmission rate for the first time – a goal that has driven our work since our creation."

a3096.speaker: Mpolokeng Mohloai, Country Director for mothers2mothers Lesotho
a3096.name: Mpolokeng Mohloai
a3096.title: Country Director for mothers2mothers Lesotho
a3096.speech: Said funding cuts from key donors like PEPFAR and USAID have directly impacted their ability to deliver services at scale ; warned: "Scaling back or discontinuing the Mentor Mothers programme would risk undoing decades of progress in preventing mother-to-child transmission of HIV" ; "Without this trusted, community-based support, we would likely see an increase in infant HIV infections, decreased treatment adherence, and lower retention in care. Women would have fewer safe spaces to seek help, and overburdened health facilities may struggle to fill the gap. The human cost – especially for women and children – would be devastating."

a3172.speaker: Fasil Hailemariam, IT director for the Food & Drugs Authority and team leader in developing the application
a3172.name: Fasil Hailemariam
a3172.title: IT director for the Food & Drugs Authority and team leader in developing the application
a3172.speech: said the team conducted pilot testing alongside employees of the Authority from the earliest stages.

a3172.speaker: Social Beyen, IT expert who runs his own IT company
a3172.name: Social Beyen
a3172.title: IT expert who runs his own IT company
a3172.speech: said launching such an application is necessary, because it is what this era demands ; said follow-up is required from the Authority in terms of updating relevant information about the drugs, adding that after the application launches, people who are illegally importing drugs and other pharmaceutical products will be easier to identify.

a3172.speaker: Abera Denke, communications director at the Food & Drugs Authority
a3172.name: Abera Denke
a3172.title: communications director at the Food & Drugs Authority
a3172.speech: said that for a company wishing to import drugs, skincare products or health equipment, the registration is online, and the company will get approval after the Authority inspects the manufacturing process regarding the product.

a3353.speaker: Dr Ndeye Fatou Ndiaye, coordinator of the National Food Fortification Alliance of Senegal (ANF-Senegal)
a3353.name: Dr Ndeye Fatou Ndiaye
a3353.title: coordinator of the National Food Fortification Alliance of Senegal (ANF-Senegal)
a3353.speech: Appreciates that the Regional Alliance comes at just the right time to boost the work of the existing national food fortification alliances and their operationalisation in countries that do not have them, in order to guarantee the implementation of ECOWAS recommendations. ; "We commit to supporting this regional alliance, by first creating a virtual platform for communication and sharing of experiences, a framework for exchanges among all the NFAs with regular meetings," she promises on behalf of her peers.

a3353.speaker: Shawn Baker, director of programmes at Helen Keller Intl (HKI), speaking on behalf of the technical and financial partners
a3353.name: Shawn Baker
a3353.title: director of programmes at Helen Keller Intl (HKI), speaking on behalf of the technical and financial partners
a3353.speech: Gives assurance that they will contribute to mobilising the resources necessary to make the alliances function, to strengthen the system for implementing large-scale fortification in the region and to improve the synergy of actions among partners.

a3353.speaker: Rodrigue Kohoun, technical adviser to Benin's Minister of Health
a3353.name: Rodrigue Kohoun
a3353.title: technical adviser to Benin's Minister of Health
a3353.speech: "The results emerging from the work are laudable"; notes that the "fruitful" exchanges highlighted the need to strengthen the availability of premixes and equipment for food fortification through incentive measures, and to revitalise the national alliances while strengthening public-private partnership and the monitoring of interventions in this area.

a3353.speaker: Bernard Toni, rapporteur, Catholic Relief Services (CRS)
a3353.name: Bernard Toni
a3353.title: rapporteur, Catholic Relief Services (CRS)
a3353.speech: Adds that participants emphasised strengthening the capacities of national laboratories to ensure quality control of fortified products at the national level and the integration of fortification data into the overall monitoring and evaluation system at national and regional levels.

a3403.speaker: Cuban state press
a3403.name: Cuban state press
a3403.speech: According to the state press, Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel dismissed the Minister of the Economy on Friday, after a delay in the already announced increase in fuel and transport prices.

a3403.speaker: Daniel Bessa, economist
a3403.name: Daniel Bessa
a3403.title: economist
a3403.speech: Considers that the current economic situation, resulting from the pandemic, is worse than a "war situation, both in terms of the halt in production and with regard to the capacity to recover."

a3403.speaker: Government of Cape Verde
a3403.name: Government of Cape Verde
a3403.speech: Said today that Cape Verde will receive, by the end of the year, a visit from two Russian investors interested in the fisheries sector, who want at least two vessels flying the archipelago's flag as well as a fish-processing plant for the domestic market and for export.

a3441.speaker: Jonas Banda, third-year education student at the University of Malawi (open letter to the Minister of Education)
a3441.name: Jonas Banda
a3441.title: third-year education student at the University of Malawi (open letter to the Minister of Education)
a3441.speech: Writes with great concern about "the silent yet worsening crisis that private schools in our country are facing"; says private schools have played an instrumental role in complementing the efforts of the government to provide quality education, offering many families an alternative to overcrowded and underfunded public schools, but that these institutions are now facing severe financial difficulties that threaten their very existence.

a3441.speaker: Jonas Banda, third-year education student at the University of Malawi (open letter)
a3441.name: Jonas Banda
a3441.title: third-year education student at the University of Malawi (open letter)
a3441.speech: Says that between 2020 and 2025 the cost of living in Malawi has soared, with the same sugar that cost K750 in 2020 now priced at K4000, leaving schools "caught between a rock and a hard place"; says what makes the situation even more dire is the loss of financial support from many families whose livelihoods are tied to NGOs, particularly those who depended on USAID funding — "With the withdrawal of USAID from Malawi, many parents can no longer afford to keep their children enrolled in private schools" — resulting in a sharp decline in enrollment, schools unable to pay teachers, and others being forced to shut their doors in silence.

a3441.speaker: Jonas Banda, third-year education student at the University of Malawi (open letter)
a3441.name: Jonas Banda
a3441.title: third-year education student at the University of Malawi (open letter)
a3441.speech: Urges the Minister to engage with the Private Schools Association of Malawi (PRISAM) to understand the challenges they face and to explore possible solutions that will allow them to continue operating; argues that government intervention is not just necessary but crucial, and that if the schools are allowed to fail the future of many students who rely on them is jeopardised.

a3479.speaker: Turkish government
a3479.name: Turkish government
a3479.speech: Accuses U.S.-based cleric Fethullah Gulen of orchestrating the 2016 coup attempt and designates his movement as the Fethullahist Terrorist Organization, or FETO.

a3479.speaker: Maarif official (anonymous)
a3479.name: Maarif official (anonymous)
a3479.speech: "We train students not only to succeed in Somalia but to thrive globally."

a3479.speaker: Maarif school officials
a3479.name: Maarif school officials
a3479.speech: Say the goal is to equip Somali youth with the tools needed to compete on the global stage.

a3479.speaker: Abdishakur Abullarhi, former Maarif student
a3479.name: Abdishakur Abullarhi
a3479.title: former Maarif student
a3479.speech: "Maarif gave me the foundation I needed to study abroad. Now I'm back and working to give something back to my country."

a3479.speaker: Abdallah Nurdin Mohamed, Norwegian-born former student
a3479.name: Abdallah Nurdin Mohamed
a3479.title: Norwegian-born former student
a3479.speech: Said the school helped him integrate linguistically and culturally after returning to Somalia: "When I arrived, I didn't speak Arabic and barely knew English. Maarif helped me learn both, and I even picked up Turkish."

a3479.speaker: A mother of a Maarif student (anonymous)
a3479.name: A mother of a Maarif student (anonymous)
a3479.speech: "I was displaced from Bakool and couldn't afford school fees. Without Maarif, my son would still be at home like so many other children."

a3679.speaker: Ali Othmen, independent international political analyst (op-ed author)
a3679.name: Ali Othmen
a3679.title: independent international political analyst (op-ed author)
a3679.speech: Argues that the Ukrainian parliament's 5 May revision of the law lifting restrictions on arms exports “opens Pandora's box”, creating a channel through which weapons received as humanitarian aid “for defence against aggression” become an instrument of terror on another continent, with Côte d'Ivoire becoming the main transhipment point for Ukrainian weapons resold onward to terrorist groups across Africa.

a3679.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a3679.name: Experts (unnamed)
a3679.speech: Note unanimously that there will be many buyers for these weapons, but that these buyers will certainly be far from official governmental structures; according to information from experts, the generals of the Ukrainian Armed Forces decommission up to 70% of firearms and the presidency keeps these operations under wraps, receiving their share of the profit.

a3679.speaker: Observers (unnamed)
a3679.name: Observers (unnamed)
a3679.speech: According to observers, the source of the new flow of weapons raises no question: all the alarming indications point towards Ukraine.

a3679.speaker: Internal sources in Côte d'Ivoire (anonymous)
a3679.name: Internal sources in Côte d'Ivoire (anonymous)
a3679.speech: Confirmed that it is Côte d'Ivoire that is becoming the main transhipment point for Ukrainian weapons; the author's investigation obtained a document presented as a “commercial offer” to Côte d'Ivoire in which the Ukrainian side proposes substantial arms deliveries.

a3679.speaker: Experts, former military intelligence agents
a3679.name: Experts
a3679.title: former military intelligence agents
a3679.speech: Note that it is particularly through Côte d'Ivoire that this lethal cargo is then distributed across the continent.

a3679.speaker: United Nations (data)
a3679.name: United Nations (data)
a3679.speech: According to UN data, up to 5 million pieces of unregistered weapons already circulate in clandestine networks, and Ukrainian mortars and missiles are found in the hands of terrorists in Niger and Mali.

a3679.speaker: Local social media users in AES countries
a3679.name: Local social media users in AES countries
a3679.speech: Express their discontent and their fear regarding the resurgence of terrorists, accusing Ukrainian armed “generosity” of being to blame.

a3697.speaker: Jean-Pierre Rousseau, Project Director at Winrock International, USAID
a3697.name: Jean-Pierre Rousseau
a3697.title: Project Director at Winrock International, USAID
a3697.speech: Stated during the national agricultural extension service impact-sharing workshop held in Abuja that USAID, through its Feed the Future Agricultural Extension and Advisory Services Activity in Nigeria, has supported 311 Micro, Small, and Medium-sized Enterprises (MSMEs) in providing extension services to farmers ; explained that USAID’s ‘Innovative Market-led Extension Delivery’ approach is driven by private sector engagement, with a key focus on partnering with MSMEs and other private sector actors to test, adapt, and scale effective agricultural practices for smallholder farmers in seven Nigerian states ; said USAID has identified “Most Impactful Practices” (MIPs), which are market-aligned solutions designed to sustainably improve smallholder farmers’ access to agricultural inputs, markets, and extension messaging.

a3697.speaker: Abubakar Kyari, Minister of Agriculture and Food Security
a3697.name: Abubakar Kyari
a3697.title: Minister of Agriculture and Food Security
a3697.speech: Emphasised the vital role of agricultural extension services in transforming Nigeria’s agriculture sector.

a3736.speaker: Bank of Tanzania, September 2025 report
a3736.name: Bank of Tanzania
a3736.title: September 2025 report
a3736.speech: Reported that Zanzibar recorded service receipts of USD 1,267.5 million in the year ending August 2025, a 30.6 percent increase compared to the same period in 2024, driven largely by growth in tourism as arrivals rose 26.1 percent to 861,962 visitors; that the current account surplus rose 42.1 percent to USD 673.3 million, with exports of USD 1,300.1 million against imports of USD 648.0 million; and that clove exports dropped sharply to USD 3.57 million from USD 28.75 million.

a3822.speaker: Antony Blinken, U.S. Secretary of State
a3822.name: Antony Blinken
a3822.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a3822.speech: On January 23, during the first official visit by a U.S. Secretary of State to the African Development Bank while visiting Côte d’Ivoire, praised “the… (quote truncated in the article).

a3822.speaker: Marie-Laure Akin-Olugbade, African Development Bank Vice President for Regional Development, Integration and Service Delivery
a3822.name: Marie-Laure Akin-Olugbade
a3822.title: African Development Bank Vice President for Regional Development, Integration and Service Delivery
a3822.speech: Said after her official visit to South Sudan: “We commend the Government of South Sudan for the excellent performance of its portfolio and reiterate the Bank’s commitment to supporting increased agricultural production and productivity to strengthen food security.”

a3822.speaker: Marie-Laure Akin-Olugbade, African Development Bank Vice President for Regional Development, Integration and Service Delivery
a3822.name: Marie-Laure Akin-Olugbade
a3822.title: African Development Bank Vice President for Regional Development, Integration and Service Delivery
a3822.speech: Said after policy dialogue in the Republic of Congo: “We reviewed the business environment situation in Congo and took good measure of the opportunities, challenges, and constraints that the private sector might face regarding the government’s objective to have it contribute 60-70% to the financing and implementation of the 2022-2026 National Development Plan. It was important to examine ways in which the African Development Bank could support the private sector in this ambition.”

a3822.speaker: Kevin Urama, African Development Bank Group Chief Economist and Vice President
a3822.name: Kevin Urama
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group Chief Economist and Vice President
a3822.speech: Presented the key findings of the 2024 edition of “Africa’s Macroeconomic Performance and Outlook”: “The growth of Africa’s best-performing economies has benefited from several factors, including reduced dependence on commodities through economic diversification, increased strategic investments in key growth sectors, higher public and private consumption, and positive developments in major export markets.”

a3822.speaker: William Ruto, Kenyan President
a3822.name: William Ruto
a3822.title: Kenyan President
a3822.speech: On May 12 called for a USD 25 billion ADF-17 replenishment and highlighted the impact of the Bank Group’s concessional financing window on his country’s development, telling Akinwumi Adesina in Nairobi: “I will continue to advocate vigorously for the ADF-17 replenishment. Kenya has benefited from resources made available by the Fund.”

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: During the 50th anniversary celebrations of the Islamic Development Bank, expressed gratitude to Saudi Arabia for “its support, dedication, and kindness” toward Africa, with financing touching numerous projects impacting daily lives across the continent.

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: At the Annual Meetings in Nairobi launched ten strong ideas to strengthen regional integration and development in Africa: “African people expect concrete actions from our meeting here in Nairobi. African integration is everyone’s business,” and called for a series of reforms without which it will be impossible to create what he calls a “fit-for-purpose bank.”

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: Declared of the Board of Governors’ approval of a USD 117 billion general callable capital increase: “This is a major demonstration of the faith and confidence our shareholders place in us, and our ability to use our resources well,” to “maintain and leverage our firepower while preserving our rating.”

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: Called on Korea, at the Korea-Africa Summit, to contribute to the ADF-17 replenishment and to the Alliance for Green Infrastructure in Africa (AGIA).

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: On Benin’s pledge to the African Development Fund, emphasized: “Our ambition is to encourage more African countries to become contributing states to the Fund’s resources,” citing Kenya’s pledge of USD 20 million to the Fund as an example.

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: Said of the donor loan agreement with JICA: “We could not have succeeded with the ADF-16 replenishment without Japan’s constant support for concessional donor loans. It’s important to sign these agreements, but it’s the lives we impact that matter. We keep our promises. We keep our word.”

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: Maintained at the 2024 Borlaug Dialogue in Des Moines, where he and World Bank President Ajay Banga renewed their institutions’ commitment to ending food insecurity in Africa: “Nothing is more important than feeding the world. Multilateral development banks play an important role in this.”

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: Declared at the launch of the Bank’s 60th anniversary celebrations on September 10: “I would like to salute and congratulate the Bank’s staff for their exemplary dedication. You make the Bank proud. And I am very proud of you.”

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: Described the USD 29.2 billion in expressions of interest at the Africa Investment Forum 2024 Market Days as “truly exceptional,” specifying in his closing speech: “Investors and project sponsors met in 41 boardrooms to review, discuss, and commit to 37 investment projects. These projects cover transport, electricity, energy, agribusiness, industry, mining, pharmaceuticals, private equity, tourism, urban infrastructure, water management, and water and sanitation.”

a3822.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a3822.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3822.title: African Development Bank Group President
a3822.speech: Expressed gratitude to Côte d’Ivoire’s President Alassane Ouattara and the Ivorian government for their support of the Bank’s new headquarters project: “The decision taken by our Boards of Directors shows the Bank’s lasting anchor in Côte d’Ivoire, our home, today and tomorrow. We count on the resolute support of the Ivorian government to accompany us in this historic project.”

a3822.speaker: Solomon Quaynor, African Development Bank Vice President for Private Sector, Infrastructure and Industrialization
a3822.name: Solomon Quaynor
a3822.title: African Development Bank Vice President for Private Sector, Infrastructure and Industrialization
a3822.speech: Stated on the USD 1 billion loan to Transnet: “Our partnership will enable Transnet to implement a comprehensive recovery plan, addressing operational inefficiencies, particularly in the rail and port sectors. This plan aligns with South Africa’s strategic roadmap for the freight logistics system and is overseen by the National Logistics Crisis Committee, chaired by the presidency. This initiative demonstrates our commitment to strengthening national logistics capabilities and promoting sustainable economic growth.”

a3822.speaker: Solomon Quaynor, African Development Bank Vice President for Private Sector, Infrastructure and Industrialization
a3822.name: Solomon Quaynor
a3822.title: African Development Bank Vice President for Private Sector, Infrastructure and Industrialization
a3822.speech: Said of the Bank’s visit to India and the pharmaceutical roundtable: “We have partnered with India Exim Bank to support Indian private sector participation in Africa’s growth, particularly in public projects that the African Development Bank finances with India Exim Bank’s export credits support.”

a3822.speaker: Nnenna Nwabufo, African Development Bank Director General for East Africa
a3822.name: Nnenna Nwabufo
a3822.title: African Development Bank Director General for East Africa
a3822.speech: Emphasized about the USD 135 million financing for the Union of Comoros: “This is a flagship project of Plan Comoros Emergent 2030 that will certainly help improve living conditions and reduce Comoros’ vulnerability to climate change.”

a3822.speaker: Kevin Kariuki, African Development Bank Vice President for Power, Energy, Climate and Green Growth
a3822.name: Kevin Kariuki
a3822.title: African Development Bank Vice President for Power, Energy, Climate and Green Growth
a3822.speech: Announced that the African Development Bank officially joined the Africa Carbon Markets Initiative effective May 30, 2024: “I am pleased to announce that the African Development Bank is now an official member of the Africa Carbon Markets Initiative. Through this decision, the Bank commits to establishing a mechanism to support carbon market initiatives across our continent.”

a3822.speaker: Kevin Kariuki, African Development Bank Vice President for Power, Energy, Climate and Green Growth
a3822.name: Kevin Kariuki
a3822.title: African Development Bank Vice President for Power, Energy, Climate and Green Growth
a3822.speech: Said after the clean cooking letter of intent signing in Antananarivo: “This is an important step to increase access to clean cooking fuels in Madagascar. Delivering essential infrastructure that saves lives and impacts climate positively is a major component of the African Development Bank’s investment strategy, and we are delighted to collaborate with Africa50, the OPEC Fund, and the Government of Madagascar to advance clean cooking in the country.”

a3822.speaker: Romuald Wadagni, Benin’s Minister of Economy and Finance
a3822.name: Romuald Wadagni
a3822.title: Benin’s Minister of Economy and Finance
a3822.speech: Announced in Cotonou on October 11, during the opening session of the ADF-16 Mid-Term Review, that Benin pledged to contribute USD 2 million to the next replenishment of the African Development Fund.

a3822.speaker: Michael D. Higgins, Irish President
a3822.name: Michael D. Higgins
a3822.title: Irish President
a3822.speech: In a speech at the 2024 “Kofi Annan Eminent Speakers” series on November 7 in Abidjan, emphasized the urgent need for global collaboration to address the interdependent crises of climate change, growing debt, and food insecurity in Africa, and noted that current Global North contributions to countries hit by climate change remain largely insufficient.

a3822.speaker: Duma Boko, Botswana’s President
a3822.name: Duma Boko
a3822.title: Botswana’s President
a3822.speech: Emphasized at the opening of the African Economic Conference in Gaborone: “Peace and stability in Africa must be anchored in responsible and responsive governance.”

a3822.speaker: Organizers of the African Economic Conference (African Development Bank, UNDP and UN Economic Commission for Africa)
a3822.name: Organizers of the African Economic Conference (African Development Bank
a3822.title: UNDP and UN Economic Commission for Africa)
a3822.speech: Called for bold reforms and decisive action to accelerate Africa’s ambition to become a global power.

a3822.speaker: TIME magazine (TIME100 Climate List)
a3822.name: TIME magazine (TIME100 Climate List)
a3822.speech: Named Hassatou Diop N’Sele one of the main “climate change catalysts” in its annual TIME100 Climate List, describing her as a climate finance pioneer and highlighting how she helped the Bank introduce a USD 750 million “hybrid” bond to increase climate financing.

a3822.speaker: Hassatou Diop N’Sele, African Development Bank Vice President for Finance and Chief Financial Officer
a3822.name: Hassatou Diop N’Sele
a3822.title: African Development Bank Vice President for Finance and Chief Financial Officer
a3822.speech: Told TIME that the bond had proven to be a viable instrument for multinational banks for the future, stating: “Unfortunately, less than 3% of our countries have access to climate funds. This is one of the reasons we decided to increase our climate financing.”

a3926.speaker: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku, professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria; former executive director of the Institute for Agricultural Research (op-ed author)
a3926.name: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku
a3926.title: professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria; former executive director of the Institute for Agricultural Research (op-ed author)
a3926.speech: Responds to personal attacks over Gates Foundation funding: “Yes, the Gates Foundation, through partners like the African Agricultural Technology Foundation (AATF), has supported this research since 2008... But let us be clear, this is collaborative science, not control. The intellectual property for Bt cowpea is held by public institutions, and Nigeria’s National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA) oversees all approvals. I have led this ‘10-year slow walk’ of local trials... I invite critics to visit our labs in Zaria. We are building Nigeria’s capacity, not surrendering it.”

a3926.speaker: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku, professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.name: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku
a3926.title: professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.speech: Argues on food sovereignty and national security: “Bt cowpea enhances sovereignty by reducing import dependency. Nigeria produces four million tons of cowpea annually. Yet, pests cost us billions in losses and force heavy pesticide use. Our GMO variety, SAMPEA 20T, cuts sprays by 80 per cent. It saves farmers money and health risks... Rather than a threat, this is empowerment. It is Nigerian-led, for Nigerian farmers.”

a3926.speaker: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku, professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.name: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku
a3926.title: professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.speech: On claims that partners like the Gates Foundation and USAID dictate policies for economic capture: “Candidly, funding comes with strings like transparency reporting. But decisions rest with us. The Gates Foundation’s support for cowpea aims at nutrition for over 200 million Africans, not profit. It is grant-based, not commercial. I have collaborated internationally, but my allegiance is to Nigeria’s smallholder farmers. If we reject all aid, how do we fund the research? Let us demand accountability, yes. But let us not dismiss tools that have lifted yields in countries like South Africa and Burkina Faso...”

a3926.speaker: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku, professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.name: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku
a3926.title: professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.speech: On regulatory capture: “Accusations that NBMA and NABDA are biased toward corporate interests erode public trust. I share concerns about transparency. It is vital. But NBMA’s process involves multi-year trials, public input, and alignment with Codex Alimentarius standards. For Bt cowpea, we conducted confined field trials across Nigeria. We proved safety before the 2019 approval. Independent audits could strengthen this. But dismissing it as ‘capture’ overlooks the science. Over 280 global institutions affirm GMO safety when regulated.”

a3926.speaker: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku, professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.name: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku
a3926.title: professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.speech: On yields: “Bt cowpea boosts yields by 20 to 30 per cent in pest-prone areas. This is verified through independent trials. Global meta-analyses confirm GM crops increase outputs while cutting inputs. We need more local studies. But the benefits are tangible for our farmers.”

a3926.speaker: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku, professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.name: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku
a3926.title: professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.speech: On media complicity claims: “I urge balanced reporting. Include critics. But let us fact-check. My interview was evidence-based, not scripted. Misinformation, like unproven health scares, harms more than helps.”

a3926.speaker: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku, professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.name: Mohammad Faguji Ishiyaku
a3926.title: professor of Plant Breeding, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
a3926.speech: On farmer dependency on patented seeds: “For Bt cowpea, this is not the case. Farmers can save and replant seeds legally. It is not under restrictive patents like some commercial hybrids. While some GMOs require contracts, ours prioritises accessibility. Reduced pesticide costs offset any expenses. This empowers smallholders I have mentored.” ; On calls for bans or moratoria: “Precaution is wise. But Bt cowpea met Codex standards and local regulations. A moratorium risks delaying solutions to hunger amid climate change.”

a3926.speaker: World Health Organisation
a3926.name: World Health Organisation
a3926.speech: States unequivocally that approved GM foods pose no greater health risks than conventional ones.

a3926.speaker: Environmental assessments by Nigeria's National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA)
a3926.name: Environmental assessments by Nigeria's National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA)

a3988.speaker: Amnesty International report, “They Raped All of Us: Sexual Violence Against Women and Girls in Sudan”
a3988.name: Amnesty International report
a3988.title: “They Raped All of Us: Sexual Violence Against Women and Girls in Sudan”
a3988.speech: Outlines how these atrocities amount to war crimes and potentially crimes against humanity ; details horrific incidents of sexual violence, including the rape or gang-rape of 36 women and girls as young as 15, across four Sudanese states between April 2023 and October 2024 ; documented cases of sexual slavery, including a woman held captive in a Khartoum house for a month, enduring daily sexual assaults ; based on interviews with 30 survivors and their relatives, mostly from Ugandan refugee camps, all of whom identified RSF fighters as the perpetrators ; highlights the inadequate global response to the crisis and that cuts to critical USAID-funded programs have reduced access to sexual health care for those affected ; calls for an urgent response from the global community to end the RSF's impunity, stop the flow of weapons to Sudan, and provide justice for the survivors.

a3988.speaker: Deprose Muchena, Amnesty International's Senior Director for Regional Human Rights Impact
a3988.name: Deprose Muchena
a3988.title: Amnesty International's Senior Director for Regional Human Rights Impact
a3988.speech: “The RSF's assaults on Sudanese women and girls are sickening, depraved, and aimed at inflicting maximum humiliation. The RSF has targeted civilians, particularly women and girls, with unimaginable cruelty during this war. The world must act to stop the RSF's atrocities by stemming the flow of weapons into Sudan, pressuring the leadership to end sexual violence, and holding perpetrators, including top commanders, accountable.”

a3988.speaker: Deprose Muchena, Amnesty International's Senior Director for Regional Human Rights Impact (on the international response)
a3988.name: Deprose Muchena
a3988.title: Amnesty International's Senior Director for Regional Human Rights Impact (on the international response)
a3988.speech: “The international response to the suffering of Sudanese women and girls has been reprehensible. The world has failed to protect civilians, provide sufficient humanitarian aid, or hold perpetrators accountable. It's time for the international community to acknowledge the truth of what has happened in Sudan, ensure justice for the victims, and offer reparations and comprehensive health care to survivors.”

a3988.speaker: Woman from Nyala, South Darfur (survivor, unnamed)
a3988.name: Woman from Nyala
a3988.title: South Darfur (survivor, unnamed)
a3988.speech: Recounted being tied to a tree and raped in front of others by RSF soldiers: “It was the most horrific day in my life.”

a3988.speaker: Woman from Madani, Gezira (survivor, unnamed)
a3988.name: Woman from Madani
a3988.title: Gezira (survivor, unnamed)
a3988.speech: “It was so humiliating. I feel broken.” — after being gang-raped by three RSF soldiers while her 12-year-old daughter and sister-in-law looked on.

a3988.speaker: Nurse in Khartoum North (survivor, unnamed female medical worker)
a3988.name: Nurse in Khartoum North (survivor
a3988.title: unnamed female medical worker)
a3988.speech: Recalled how 13 soldiers abducted her in Khartoum North, forced her to treat critically wounded men, and then gang-raped her.

a3988.speaker: Survivors of sexual violence (unnamed, interviewed by Amnesty International)
a3988.name: Survivors of sexual violence (unnamed
a3988.title: interviewed by Amnesty International)
a3988.speech: Reported that female medical workers were raped if they failed to save injured soldiers ; shared that they were targeted by RSF soldiers on suspicion of supporting the SAF ; described how resisting rape resulted in beatings, torture, or death, including the killing of an 11-year-old boy who tried to protect his mother.

a4165.speaker: Angela Muzenda, secretary of the Rubweruchena micro-irrigation scheme, Ward 11 Chivi
a4165.name: Angela Muzenda
a4165.title: secretary of the Rubweruchena micro-irrigation scheme, Ward 11 Chivi
a4165.speech: Said the garden would definitely see them achieving the President's Vision 2030 of an upper middle-income economy before 2030 ; “I want to thank those of USAID Takunda, who came into our district to assist because, before we were struggling to make ends meet but now through this irrigation facility, we are now able to look after our families. Through this irrigation scheme we now have enough water for domestic use and for our livestock.”

a4165.speaker: Angela Muzenda, secretary of the Rubweruchena micro-irrigation scheme, Ward 11 Chivi
a4165.name: Angela Muzenda
a4165.title: secretary of the Rubweruchena micro-irrigation scheme, Ward 11 Chivi
a4165.speech: “They taught us a lot of issues including those of gender-based violence and I can say the cases in our ward have dropped significantly because we are now busy with farming. Everyone is now occupied and it has not only opened opportunities to women and the youth, but also to people with disabilities.”

a4165.speaker: Tavaziva, farmer
a4165.name: Tavaziva
a4165.title: farmer
a4165.speech: Said through the project they were able to sustain their families with those from the surrounding communities admiring the progress they were making ; “I am very happy with this programme which was brought to us by those from USAID Takunda through the vision of President Mnangagwa of Vision 2030. I subscribe to the notion that Nyika inovakwa nevene vayo. Chivi is a dry area but through such initiatives we are able to produce enough food for our families.”

a4165.speaker: Walter Mwasaa, USAID Takunda Project Director and Assistant Country Director for CARE Zimbabwe
a4165.name: Walter Mwasaa
a4165.title: USAID Takunda Project Director and Assistant Country Director for CARE Zimbabwe
a4165.speech: Said for the past four years they had been working towards accelerating the vision of an upper middle-income economy by 2030 ; “Over the last four years, this project has been playing its role towards the realisation of the UN Sustainable Development Goals and significantly contributing to Zimbabwe’s Vision 2030. The vision of the Government to achieve an upper middle income by 2030 will be achieved if we also work in our rural communities and ensure that they are empowered and food secure.” ; said through the project, communities were generating employment and income through different activities that they undertake.

a4165.speaker: Walter Mwasaa, USAID Takunda Project Director and Assistant Country Director for CARE Zimbabwe
a4165.name: Walter Mwasaa
a4165.title: USAID Takunda Project Director and Assistant Country Director for CARE Zimbabwe
a4165.speech: “The United States government has given us another two years to be able to work with you as you continue to deepen the impact of this and many other gardens in the community. Our commitment is to work with you, with the Government, with the private sector to ensure that this project remains sustainable, viable, profitable and of income to each one of you.”

a4260.speaker: CAPSAT (elite military unit)
a4260.name: CAPSAT (elite military unit)
a4260.speech: Turned against President Andry Rajoelina, aligning with the protesters and declaring military control over the country.

a4260.speaker: Colonel Michael Randrianirina, leader of the military
a4260.name: Colonel Michael Randrianirina
a4260.title: leader of the military
a4260.speech: The military, under his leadership, announced a transitional period of up to two years during which they would govern alongside a provisional government, framed as a pathway to restoring order and preparing for new elections.

a4260.speaker: African Union
a4260.name: African Union
a4260.speech: Has urged restraint and adherence to constitutional mandates by the military, calling for the military to refrain from political meddling.

a4329.speaker: Government of Nigeria (decision)
a4329.name: Government of Nigeria (decision)
a4329.speech: Announced that no new federal university will be built in the next seven years, a decision intended to focus on strengthening existing universities and improving the quality of education.

a4329.speaker: Nigerian students
a4329.name: Nigerian students
a4329.speech: As the students themselves stated, the lack of quality education and financial problems are hampering the teaching and learning process in universities.

a4329.speaker: Data/statistics on Nigerian higher education
a4329.name: Data/statistics on Nigerian higher education
a4329.speech: Data indicates that currently only 12 per cent of Nigerian students who complete secondary school enter university; of the 275 universities, 199 admitted very few students this year and 34 admitted no new students at all; women account for only 21 per cent of students entering higher education in West African countries.

a4329.speaker: Sheriff Ghali Ibrahim, education affairs expert
a4329.name: Sheriff Ghali Ibrahim
a4329.title: education affairs expert
a4329.speech: Stated that attacks carried out on students in various parts of the country have created obstacles to the teaching and learning process.

a4329.speaker: Nigerian education experts
a4329.name: Nigerian education experts
a4329.speech: Said that the government’s decision is intended to free education from political and religious interference; the decision has created division among scholars in the sector, with some saying it is a step that helps ensure the quality of education while others criticise it as failing to solve the entrenched security and other problems.

a4329.speaker: Adeniyi Abiodun, education policy expert
a4329.name: Adeniyi Abiodun
a4329.title: education policy expert
a4329.speech: Stated that a balanced and carefully considered structural change is needed to sustainably solve Nigeria’s education problem; the experts added that ensuring the safety of schools, expanding access to education and making fees affordable are crucial for the teaching and learning process to succeed.

a4432.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a4432.name: Marco Rubio
a4432.title: US Secretary of State
a4432.speech: Described Rasool’s criticisms of President Trump’s policies as “unacceptable,” adding that the ambassador harboured animosity towards the US president; said on X, where he also announced the expulsion, that Rasool “hates America.”

a4432.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South Africa’s Ambassador to the US
a4432.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a4432.title: South Africa’s Ambassador to the US
a4432.speech: Told a webinar hosted by a South African think-tank that Trump was “mobilising a supremacism” and also trying to “project white victimhood as a dog whistle” and reaction to the demographic reality of a diminishing white population: “We see it in the domestic politics of the USA, the MAGA movement as a response not simply to a supremacist instinct, but to very clear data that shows great demographic shifts in the USA in which the voting electorate in the USA is projected to become 48 per cent white.”

a4432.speaker: Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs (talk during author’s visit)
a4432.name: Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs (talk during author’s visit)
a4432.speech: The talk at the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs was that South Africa took a bribe of $2 billion from Iran to mount a case against the Benjamin Netanyahu government at the International Criminal Court (ICC).

a4432.speaker: Diplomatic sources in Pretoria
a4432.name: Diplomatic sources in Pretoria
a4432.speech: Have denied the allegation that South Africa took a $2 billion bribe from Iran to mount the ICC case.

a4432.speaker: South Africa (government)
a4432.name: South Africa (government)
a4432.speech: Said it would not withdraw its case of genocide against Israel, saying it is aware that “Standing by our principles sometimes has consequences.”

a4432.speaker: Babafemi Badejo, academic and diplomat
a4432.name: Babafemi Badejo
a4432.title: academic and diplomat
a4432.speech: “South Africa has, of late, been leading many countries over Gaza-Palestine. About four-fifths of African countries are, at best, lukewarm on this issue. It’s not a surprise that African countries have been mute over the US Secretary of State’s action declaring the South African ambassador persona non grata.” ; “Fear of punishments and resignation to a life of minimal relevance, if at all, has been the stance of many African countries. How does a Lilliputian state begging for food aid for its people assert itself.”

a4432.speaker: Multichoice
a4432.name: Multichoice
a4432.speech: Said the cut in subscription fees in South Africa was a token to subscribers for the cost of living crisis, while attributing the increase in Nigeria to inflation and infrastructure.

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Reaffirmed the ANC's commitment to the values and principles to which so many of our legends dedicated their lives; said the core ideal that is the reason for the ANC's existence - the creation of a united, non-racial, non-sexist, democratic, prosperous and equitable society - is yet to be fully realised, and committed that the newly elected leadership "shall remain faithful and diligent custodians of this glorious vision."

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Said that this year, as the centenary of the birth of Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela is celebrated, "we shall intensify our efforts to realise his vision of a united South Africa in which all live in peace with equal rights and opportunities"; that the ANC shall "redouble our efforts to build a society in which black poverty and white privilege are consigned to the past" and place at the top of its agenda "Madiba's vision of a non-sexist society."

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Said that at the centre of all the ANC's efforts this year must be the fundamental renewal and revitalisation of the African National Congress; that the 54th National Conference recognised that "the movement has become deeply divided through factionalism, patronage, corruption and competition for resources," that structures have been weakened and the confidence of the people in the ANC eroded, and that Conference decided the ANC should embark with immediate effect on a far-reaching programme of organisation-building and renewal.

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Said that despite the attention given to socio-economic transformation "our economy has not performed well" - economic growth has remained low, unemployment high, levels of investment have dropped, the budget is under pressure, business and consumer confidence is low and the country has suffered credit rating downgrades; that the economy "has also been severely undermined by corruption and state capture, institutional instability, policy inconsistency, poor performance of state-owned enterprises and a sense of drift within the ANC."

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Said the ANC aims to forge a social pact between government, labour, business and communities urgently to reignite economic growth and accelerate transformation, focusing in particular on youth unemployment; announced the implementation of free higher education for students from poor and working class backgrounds whose household income is less than R350,000, through full bursaries at public TVET colleges and universities, with existing NSFAS loans converted into full bursaries.

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Said the ANC reaffirms the role, mandate and independence of the Reserve Bank and, as mandated by Conference, "we call on government to develop proposals, in line with international practice, to ensure full public ownership of the Bank"; said the mandate of the competition authorities will be expanded to reduce monopoly control of the economy and increase competition.

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Said there was overwhelming support at the 54th National Conference that "the ANC must pursue the expropriation of land without compensation," to be done in a manner that meets the constitutional requirement of redress while promoting economic development, agricultural production and food security.

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Said the ANC welcomes the announcement by President Jacob Zuma of the establishment of a commission of inquiry in line with the findings of the Public Protector's report on state capture; that anti-corruption efforts must be more effectively coordinated and all forms of corruption exposed and prosecuted, and that the country's intelligence services, police and prosecutorial authorities should be strengthened and fortified to act with professionalism, "and without fear, favour or prejudice."

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Said the ANC will intensify efforts to improve health, that "we must never accept as permanent or irreversible our status as the country with the world's biggest HIV epidemic," and called for decisive steps to end the epidemic by implementing the 90-90-90 strategy, adding two million more people to the antiretroviral treatment programme; called on South Africans, in the context of the listeriosis outbreak, "to heed the advice of the World Health Organization and the Department of Health."

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Said the ANC reaffirms the inalienable right of the people of Western Sahara to self-determination and independence; condemns the withdrawal of Morocco from the UN-led peace process and calls on the UN to bring all parties back to the negotiating table; will continue supporting the peace process in Sudan and South Sudan; reaffirms its commitment to give practical support to the oppressed people of Palestine and holds the firm view that the downgrade of the South African embassy in Israel to a Liaison Office would send a strong signal; and calls on the South African government to increase trade with Cuba and on the United States "to remove the illegal economic embargo against Cuba."

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Set out the priority tasks for the movement for 2018: a deliberate programme of organisational renewal getting rid of "gate-keeping, vote buying and undue interference"; restoring the integrity and credibility of the ANC and strengthening the Integrity Commission; bringing the ANC closer to the people; uniting all South Africans around a shared vision of fundamental transformation; mobilising social partners behind an economic recovery plan; confronting corruption and state capture, including the immediate establishment of a commission of inquiry; restoring the credibility of public institutions; developing an affordable and sustainable funding model for free higher education; and implementing a comprehensive approach to land reform, with the NEC to develop proposals on expropriation of land without compensation.

a4573.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4573.title: ANC President (January 8th Statement)
a4573.speech: Announced that the NEC declares 2018 as '100 YEARS OF NELSON MANDELA: THE YEAR OF RENEWAL, UNITY AND JOBS,' and honoured the activists who passed away over the past year, dipping the ANC's banner in honour of Ahmed Kathrada, Major General Mxolisi Petane, Sindiso Magaqa, Emma Mashinini, Essa Moosa, Laloo Isu Chiba, Mochubela Seekoe, Ronnie Mamoepa, Kay Moonsamy, John Ncinane, John Pilane, Reverend Jakes Alberts, Andimba Toivo ya Toivo and Keorapetse Kgositsile among others.

a4573.speaker: Nelson Mandela, former President (quoted in the statement)
a4573.name: Nelson Mandela
a4573.title: former President (quoted in the statement)
a4573.speech: Quoted as saying that political freedom goes side by side with 'freedom from hunger, want and suffering.'

a4573.speaker: World Health Organization and the Department of Health
a4573.name: World Health Organization and the Department of Health
a4573.speech: Have five key commandments for food safety: to keep clean and wash hands before and while preparing food; to separate raw and cooked food; to cook food properly; to keep food at safe temperatures; and to use safe water and raw materials.

a4573.speaker: National Development Plan
a4573.name: National Development Plan
a4573.speech: Noted that South Africa remains a highly unequal society where too many people live in poverty and too few have access to economic opportunities.

a4630.speaker: Dr. Jeanne Ndayishimiye, provincial doctor in Muramvya
a4630.name: Dr. Jeanne Ndayishimiye
a4630.title: provincial doctor in Muramvya
a4630.speech: According to her, the partnership with Belgium worked actively on health infrastructure and equipment - the construction and equipping of the Muramvya health centre-maternity unit, the rehabilitation and extension of Kiganda hospital, and the upgrading of health centres that did not meet health standards. "The support for improving the quality of health facilities as well as the digitalisation of health services have made it possible to improve the quality of services." ; Specified that 7 health centres in Muramvya province are already digitalised, which has allowed revenues to increase by up to 300% and made statistical data reliable.

a4630.speaker: Dr. Jeanne Ndayishimiye, provincial doctor in Muramvya
a4630.name: Dr. Jeanne Ndayishimiye
a4630.title: provincial doctor in Muramvya
a4630.speech: Regretted that despite this progress challenges persist, deploring above all the recurrent shortage of drinking water at Muramvya district hospital, the lack of doctors, and the absence of a blood bank in the two districts.

a4630.speaker: Dr. Jeanne Ndayishimiye, provincial doctor in Muramvya
a4630.name: Dr. Jeanne Ndayishimiye
a4630.title: provincial doctor in Muramvya
a4630.speech: Highlighted the interventions carried out by the Belgian NGO Medecins sans vacances, a partner of Enabel in Burundi, citing among others the donation of two ambulances to the Muramvya and Kiganda health districts, the training of providers in mental health, the donation of two ultrasound machines and intensive care service rooms.

a4630.speaker: Provincial health directorate of Muramvya
a4630.name: Provincial health directorate of Muramvya
a4630.speech: Testified to the progress brought about by the partnership between the Kingdom of Belgium and Burundi: "Satisfaction rates with services have risen sharply. Training in district surgery, for example, saw an improvement of 74% in 2022 compared with 56% in 2021."

a4630.speaker: Dr Olivier Nijimbere, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry in charge of Public Health
a4630.name: Dr Olivier Nijimbere
a4630.title: Permanent Secretary of the Ministry in charge of Public Health
a4630.speech: Praised the achievements resulting from Belgian-Burundian cooperation in Muramvya province, saying health promotion will help reduce runaway population growth: "Today, there are concrete actions showing progress; we invite all actors to invest themselves too in improving health."

a4630.speaker: Jerome Nduwimana, director of the Muramvya Vocational Training Centre
a4630.name: Jerome Nduwimana
a4630.title: director of the Muramvya Vocational Training Centre
a4630.speech: Said the project focused on equipping the training workshops and strengthening the capacities of the trainers: "The support has been beneficial for the centre; before, the trainers were not well trained either in pedagogy or in technical skills." ; Also stressed the improvement in the quality of learning brought about by Enabel's ACFPT project.

a4630.speaker: Management of the Muramvya Vocational Training Centre
a4630.name: Management of the Muramvya Vocational Training Centre
a4630.speech: Requested that the support be extended to all the streams, noting that Enabel covers only 5 of the 7 streams the centre offers (masonry, carpentry, sewing, office automation, welding, automotive mechanics and electricity).

a4630.speaker: Heidy Rombouts, Director General of Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid, Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4630.name: Heidy Rombouts
a4630.title: Director General of Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid, Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4630.speech: Praised the work done by Enabel in the health facilities of Muramvya and Kiganda and in the Muramvya Vocational Training Centre: "We are very pleased with the achievements, but what is important is the permanence and sustainability of the interventions" - hence, according to her, the importance of integrating young people into economic life to ensure the durability of these gains.

a4630.speaker: Heidy Rombouts, Director General of Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid, Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4630.name: Heidy Rombouts
a4630.title: Director General of Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid, Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4630.speech: "The construction of the office of the northern district of Bujumbura aims to support the health sector by focusing on investments and infrastructure, with equipment constituting a central pillar of health that contributes to the quality of care." ; Announced a bilateral partnership cooperation programme worth 75 million euros for the period 2024 to 2028, stressing that a significant part of it will be focused on the health sector ; Encouraged the beneficiaries of support to take ownership of the gains of these interventions and reaffirmed the Kingdom of Belgium's commitment to work in close collaboration with Burundi to achieve that sustainability.

a4630.speaker: Dr Lydwine Baradahana, Minister of Public Health and the Fight against AIDS
a4630.name: Dr Lydwine Baradahana
a4630.title: Minister of Public Health and the Fight against AIDS
a4630.speech: "This building attests once again to solidarity and cooperation in the public health sector." ; Specified that the office was built within the framework of the Burundi-Belgium partnership under its programme of support for infrastructure, equipment and maintenance, PAISS, component 5 ; Said the health office will make it possible to improve the quality and quantity of health care and to address challenges such as the insufficiency of infrastructure and equipment in health facilities, especially in maintenance, using local means to protect the environment.

a4630.speaker: Dr Lydwine Baradahana, Minister of Public Health and the Fight against AIDS
a4630.name: Dr Lydwine Baradahana
a4630.title: Minister of Public Health and the Fight against AIDS
a4630.speech: Encouraged the Kingdom of Belgium to extend its intervention to the national level and concentrate efforts in the municipality of Bujumbura, pleading above all for the continuation of actions in biomedical maintenance, training in district surgery and the digitalisation of health facilities.

a4630.speaker: Dr Lydwine Baradahana, Minister of Public Health and the Fight against AIDS
a4630.name: Dr Lydwine Baradahana
a4630.title: Minister of Public Health and the Fight against AIDS
a4630.speech: Recommended to the new occupants of the office: "I ask the staff of this district to maintain these premises well and to complete what remains in order to ensure the cleanliness of the building."

a4776.speaker: Josh Lipsky, chair of international economics at the Atlantic Council
a4776.name: Josh Lipsky
a4776.title: chair of international economics at the Atlantic Council
a4776.speech: “I think it's problematic not to have the world's largest economy represented at the table, at least at a senior political level” ; “It raises questions about the G20's long-term viability,” adding that Bessent's absence foreshadowed U.S. plans for a slimmed-down, “back to basics” G20 when it assumes the grouping's rotating presidency next year.

a4776.speaker: Fundi Tshazibana, South African Reserve Bank Deputy Governor
a4776.name: Fundi Tshazibana
a4776.title: South African Reserve Bank Deputy Governor
a4776.speech: “Policy uncertainty is the biggest theme at this point in time,” told Reuters.

a4776.speaker: Brad Setser, Council on Foreign Relations
a4776.name: Brad Setser
a4776.title: Council on Foreign Relations
a4776.speech: “The G20 was built around a presumption that all the world's major economies shared a common interest in a stable, relatively open global economy. But Trump doesn't really care about stability and wants a more closed global economy.”

a4776.speaker: Goldman Sachs
a4776.name: Goldman Sachs
a4776.speech: Sub-Saharan Africa's external debt has ballooned to $800 billion, or 45% of GDP, according to Goldman Sachs.

a4776.speaker: Trevor Manuel, former finance minister of South Africa, leading the Africa Expert Panel of the G20
a4776.name: Trevor Manuel
a4776.title: former finance minister of South Africa, leading the Africa Expert Panel of the G20
a4776.speech: “The views that they've expressed are if you negotiate them down before taking the loan, they will go with that” ; “But once the loan is made, then they expect a return, and that is embedded in their legislation. So that is one issue that needs a lot of attention” ; said China's Belt and Road Initiative has brought very significant resources to the African continent, “but there are also the offsets” ; “I think that part of the push going forward is greater transparency, which means that some of the barter arrangements and so on need to be dealt with quite differently.”

a4776.speaker: Lumkile Mondi, political commentator at the University of Witwatersrand
a4776.name: Lumkile Mondi
a4776.title: political commentator at the University of Witwatersrand
a4776.speech: “Africa is in a difficult space” ; “Investment in the continent is going to dwindle because of high levels of indebtedness and low GDP growth, making it less relevant in the current geoeconomics.”

a4776.speaker: South African National Treasury
a4776.name: South African National Treasury
a4776.speech: Said it was “premature to comment” on specific goals for the gathering.

a4776.speaker: Duncan Pieterse, Director General of the South African Treasury (statement on Monday)
a4776.name: Duncan Pieterse
a4776.title: Director General of the South African Treasury (statement on Monday)
a4776.speech: Said in a statement on Monday that they hoped to issue the first Communique under the South African G20 presidency at the end of the meetings.

a4776.speaker: The G20's financial stability watchdog (Financial Stability Board)
a4776.name: The G20's financial stability watchdog (Financial Stability Board)
a4776.speech: On Monday delivered a new plan on how to tackle climate risks but paused policy work amid a U.S. retreat that has tested efforts to advance a united financial policy on climate-related risks.

a5043.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a5043.name: Officials (unnamed)
a5043.speech: Announced on Wednesday that the Trump administration has reversed extensive cuts to emergency food assistance for several countries, while still maintaining reductions in Afghanistan and Yemen.

a5043.speaker: Two U.N. officials (anonymous)
a5043.name: Two U.N. officials (anonymous)
a5043.speech: Said the administration notified the World Food Program (WFP) of this reversal on Tuesday. These officials requested anonymity as they were not authorized to speak to the media.

a5043.speaker: Representative of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) (anonymous)
