a5043.name: Representative of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) (anonymous)
a5043.speech: Confirmed that Jeremy Lewin, an associate of Musk responsible for the restructuring of USAID, had instructed the reinstatement of some contract terminations made over the weekend, following a report by the Associated Press regarding the cuts.

a5043.speaker: World Food Program (WFP)
a5043.name: World Food Program (WFP)
a5043.speech: Announced on Monday that it had been informed of USAID's decision to reduce funding for its emergency food program in 14 countries.

a5043.speaker: Mohamed Elmi Afrah, seasoned aid worker and political analyst
a5043.name: Mohamed Elmi Afrah
a5043.title: seasoned aid worker and political analyst
a5043.speech: "The individuals who will be most affected include mothers, nursing women, and children, among others. These are the vulnerable groups who rely heavily on aid as a primary source of livelihood."

a5043.speaker: Mustafa Diriye, logistics manager at Lusidle Petroleum and Logistics LTD, a WFP contractor
a5043.name: Mustafa Diriye
a5043.title: logistics manager at Lusidle Petroleum and Logistics LTD, a WFP contractor
a5043.speech: Expressed his shock at the initial news of the cuts: "This was entirely unexpected, and the immediate impact on us has been profound."

a5043.speaker: WFP Somalia office (post on X)
a5043.name: WFP Somalia office (post on X)
a5043.speech: Issued a warning about the severe repercussions of potential funding cuts: "U.S. funding has been essential for food assistance in Somalia, enabling WFP to meet 90% of critical hunger needs. If these cuts go through, WFP will have to halt assistance by next month, putting 620,000 individuals at risk of extreme hunger."

a5043.speaker: United Nations
a5043.name: United Nations
a5043.speech: Reported that over 6 million people in Somalia are currently experiencing acute food insecurity.

a5043.speaker: Trump administration
a5043.name: Trump administration
a5043.speech: Has criticized the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) for promoting liberal agendas and has labeled foreign aid as a misuse of resources.

a5043.speaker: U.S. officials
a5043.name: U.S. officials
a5043.speech: Have not yet responded to inquiries for comments.

a5043.speaker: Tammy Bruce, State Department spokesperson
a5043.name: Tammy Bruce
a5043.title: State Department spokesperson
a5043.speech: Acknowledged on Tuesday that some program cuts were made in error and confirmed that funding has been reinstated, though she did not provide further details.

a5072.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a5072.name: Peter H. Vrooman
a5072.title: U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a5072.speech: "This American Shelf is a tangible testament to our strong partnership with Eduardo Mondlane University," said Ambassador Vrooman during the inauguration ceremony. "We look forward to expanding access to English, broadening opportunities for educational, cultural, and professional exchanges, and connecting with Mozambican youth and academics."

a5531.speaker: Patrice Talon, President of Benin (electoral platform/société project)
a5531.name: Patrice Talon
a5531.title: President of Benin (electoral platform/société project)
a5531.speech: His platform is the only one to have specified a sub-sectoral objective of raising cotton production beyond 500,000 tonnes; the President also promises that the cotton sector will become the driving force in the use of agricultural machinery.

a5531.speaker: IMANI Francophone (think tank)
a5531.name: IMANI Francophone (think tank)
a5531.speech: Proposes avenues of support to accompany the revitalisation of the cotton sector, which is currently at the heart of the economic activity of more than 3 million Beninese.

a5531.speaker: Africa Region study (World Bank)
a5531.name: Africa Region study (World Bank)
a5531.speech: A study by the Africa Region stresses that under a monopolistic regime, Benin’s cotton sub-sector will continue to generate losses for stakeholders unless it is indefinitely subsidised by the State.

a5531.speaker: OXFAM (2001 study)
a5531.name: OXFAM (2001 study)
a5531.speech: An OXFAM study revealed in 2001 that Benin lost $33 million (double the foreign aid over the same period) because of United States subsidy policies.

a5531.speaker: Cellule d’analyse des politiques de développement (CAPOD) (2012 study)
a5531.name: Cellule d’analyse des politiques de développement (CAPOD) (2012 study)
a5531.speech: According to a study carried out by CAPOD in 2012, no less than 75% of government investment and stakeholder-support efforts are mobilised and absorbed in reviving the cotton agricultural sub-sector.

a5531.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries of Benin (figures)
a5531.name: Ministry of Agriculture
a5531.title: Livestock and Fisheries of Benin (figures)
a5531.speech: According to the Ministry’s figures, more than 93 billion CFA francs in subsidies were allocated to the cotton sector between 2011 and 2015.

a5531.speaker: Alan Akakpo, IMANI Francophone (author)
a5531.name: Alan Akakpo
a5531.title: IMANI Francophone (author)
a5531.speech: Argues that Benin as a poor country must understand that subsidies are not miracle solutions and constitute a heavy financial burden for the government; that there is so far no positive link between increases in subsidies and improvement in the economic power of cotton producers; that subsidies should be allocated wisely to benefit poor cotton producers, with an intelligent balance between subsidies and social protection for farmers; and that, to prevent corruption, the President could show good will by making public the list of beneficiaries of the subsidies to be allocated. He also urges the incoming government to invest in creating think tanks to produce informed alternatives to public policy, and to support both government and independent research alongside institutes such as the National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin.

a5700.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5700.name: Marco Rubio
a5700.title: US Secretary of State
a5700.speech: In an interview with SiriusXM Patriot on Monday, he noted that certain humanitarian programs, such as the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), which targets HIV/AIDS in Africa, will continue, while others considered ineffective or misaligned with U.S. interests may be cut; emphasized the importance of reviewing public fund allocations ; “We are going to eliminate those that do not make sense while maintaining or even expanding those that do” ; “We are not moving away from foreign aid; we are moving away from aid that is wasteful and doesn’t serve U.S. interests.”

a5700.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5700.name: Marco Rubio
a5700.title: US Secretary of State
a5700.speech: reiterated his support for PEPFAR, describing it as a vital program in the fight against HIV ; “I’m a supporter of PEPFAR. I’ve been a member of Congress, and now I’m Secretary of State. It’s a program we aim to continue”; however, he also noted that the goal of the program should be to reduce its scope over time as fewer individuals contract HIV or transmit it to their children.

a5700.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5700.name: Marco Rubio
a5700.title: US Secretary of State
a5700.speech: clarified that some forms of humanitarian aid would remain, especially when they address security concerns ; “Issues such as whether famine could destabilize a country and create a situation favorable to radical jihadists or other opportunistic groups are critical. We will continue to respond to those needs”; criticized the extensive interpretation of humanitarian aid, suggesting that certain costs should not be borne by American taxpayers ; “That doesn’t mean these are bad ideas; they just shouldn’t rely on American taxpayer funding.”

a5700.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a5700.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a5700.speech: has announced the suspension of several humanitarian operations due to the abrupt end of U.S. funding, jeopardizing aid to about 1.6 million people, including those in Burkina Faso and Sudan.

a5803.speaker: Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority, in partnership with USAID and Feed the Future Ethiopia Value Chain (FTFE-VCA)
a5803.name: Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority
a5803.title: in partnership with USAID and Feed the Future Ethiopia Value Chain (FTFE-VCA)
a5803.speech: announced that the Cup of Excellence (COE) will be held in Ethiopia for the first time in March 2020. The COE will highlight Ethiopian coffee and stimulate new market opportunities for smallholder producers in the country.

a6018.speaker: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) (World Press Freedom Index report)
a6018.name: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) (World Press Freedom Index report)
a6018.speech: According to the latest report, press freedom around the world is under greater threat than ever before, and for the first time in history its World Press Freedom Index classifies the global state of press freedom as "difficult" ; Its annual press freedom ranking finds Europe is home to the most press freedom in the world, though Southern and Eastern Europe represent some of the continent's weak spots, with the top 15 countries all in Europe and Norway scoring the highest, followed by Estonia, the Netherlands, Sweden, Finland and Denmark.

a6018.speaker: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
a6018.name: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
a6018.speech: Said that in the Middle East, dozens of reporters have been killed during Israel's military assault in Gaza.

a6018.speaker: Media freedom watchdog (unnamed)
a6018.name: Media freedom watchdog (unnamed)
a6018.speech: Has said Palestine has become the world's most dangerous state for journalists amid Israel's war on Gaza, with dozens of reporters likely killed specifically due to their work.

a6018.speaker: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
a6018.name: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
a6018.speech: Added that the United States fell two places to 57 and that President Donald Trump's administration is bringing about a "troubling deterioration" through funding cuts to public media and foreign aid.

a6351.speaker: Democratic Republic of Congo (government declaration)
a6351.name: Democratic Republic of Congo (government declaration)
a6351.speech: Declared an outbreak of Ebola virus disease in south-central Kasai province after 28 suspected cases and 15 deaths, including four health workers, were reported.

a6351.speaker: Congo's public health ministry
a6351.name: Congo's public health ministry
a6351.speech: According to Congo's public health ministry, the outbreak began with a 34-year-old pregnant woman who was hospitalized on Aug. 20 in Bulape health zone and died five days later; additional cases were reported in Bulape and Mweka health zones, with patients presenting symptoms including fever, vomiting, diarrhea and hemorrhage.

a6351.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6351.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6351.speech: Said Thursday that samples tested this week at the National Institute of Biomedical Research in Kinshasa identified the strain as Ebola Zaire.

a6351.speaker: Experts
a6351.name: Experts
a6351.speech: Warned the pullback from outbreak response will complicate efforts to stop Ebola.

a6351.speaker: Anne Rimoin, epidemiologist at the University of California, Los Angeles
a6351.name: Anne Rimoin
a6351.title: epidemiologist at the University of California, Los Angeles
a6351.speech: “Global health is perpetually underfunded, and outbreak response is always run on a shoestring” ; “Ebola containment has always been a global effort. Without US engagement, the burden will fall on fewer partners and that could slow the response and cost lives.” ; said that in past outbreaks, the US provided money and technical expertise through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and USAID, training Congolese epidemiologists, bolstering laboratory capacity, and supporting vaccines and therapies, and that that's now largely absent.

a6351.speaker: Anne Rimoin, epidemiologist at the University of California, Los Angeles
a6351.name: Anne Rimoin
a6351.title: epidemiologist at the University of California, Los Angeles
a6351.speech: Said Congo's own teams have shown strength by sequencing the virus and triggering the response within days. “It's heartening to see the excellence with which the DRC team has moved so rapidly to get the critical data out there,” she said.

a6351.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6351.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6351.speech: Said a national rapid response team, joined by its experts, has been deployed to Kasai with two tons of protective gear, medical supplies and mobile lab equipment; said cases are likely to increase as transmission is ongoing.

a6351.speaker: Mohamed Janabi, WHO's regional director for Africa
a6351.name: Mohamed Janabi
a6351.title: WHO's regional director for Africa
a6351.speech: “We're acting with determination to rapidly halt the spread of the virus and protect communities” ; “Banking on the country's long-standing expertise in controlling viral disease outbreaks, we're working closely with the health authorities to quickly scale up key response measures to end the outbreak as soon as possible.”

a6351.speaker: Patrick Otim, WHO Africa health emergency officer
a6351.name: Patrick Otim
a6351.title: WHO Africa health emergency officer
a6351.speech: “This outbreak is really a reminder of the ongoing vulnerability of communities across Africa,” he told reporters Thursday; even with a case fatality rate of almost 64% “we want to stress that there is no need to panic,” Otim said; the country has “built extensive capacity and expertise in health emergency responses.”

a6351.speaker: WHO African Region (@WHOAFRO, Twitter post)
a6351.name: WHO African Region (@WHOAFRO
a6351.title: Twitter post)
a6351.speech: “Health authorities in DRC have declared an #Ebola outbreak in Kasai Province, with 28 suspected cases & 15 deaths. To rapidly scale up the response, an advance team from the Ministry of Health & @WHO has been deployed. WHO is also delivering essential supplies and equipment.”

a6784.speaker: Martin Luther King (epigraph quotation)
a6784.name: Martin Luther King (epigraph quotation)
a6784.speech: "Our lives begin to end the day we keep silent about things that matter."

a6784.speaker: Nicéphore D. Soglo, former President of Benin
a6784.name: Nicéphore D. Soglo
a6784.title: former President of Benin
a6784.speech: In an interview, launched a violent attack on Article 44, paragraph 4 of the December 1990 constitution, which states that no one may be a candidate for President of the Republic unless they are at least 40 and at most 70 years old on the date their candidacy is filed. According to him, Charles de Gaulle, Nelson Mandela and Emmanuel Macron could not have stood for president in Benin - the first two barred by the upper limit (70 years) and the last by the lower limit (40 years). Hence his reaction: "I want this aberration that is the question of age removed from the Beninese constitution as quickly as possible. It exists in no constitution in the world."

a6784.speaker: Rodrigue, character in Corneille's Le Cid (quoted)
a6784.name: Rodrigue
a6784.title: character in Corneille's Le Cid (quoted)
a6784.speech: "I am young, it is true; but in well-born souls, valour does not wait upon the number of years."

a6784.speaker: Psalm 90 (Bible)
a6784.name: Psalm 90 (Bible)
a6784.speech: "The days of our years amount to threescore and ten (70), and for the most robust to fourscore (80); and the pride they take in them is but toil and misery, for it passes quickly and we fly away."

a6784.speaker: Church canon law
a6784.name: Church canon law
a6784.speech: Holds that an age is called canonical because it is considered the minimum age which, whatever the function considered or exercised, presupposes a certain responsibility and maturity on the part of the person chosen for that function - thus one must be at least 24 to be ordained a priest, and a woman must be at least 40 to enter the service of a parish priest; the age of 70 is likewise a canonical age indicating that one is practically at one's apogee, which is why the Church considers that a person who dies at that age has accomplished their destiny.

a6784.speaker: Pierre Accoce and Pierre Rentchnick, authors of "Ces malades qui nous gouvernent" (Stock, 1976)
a6784.name: Pierre Accoce and Pierre Rentchnick
a6784.title: authors of "Ces malades qui nous gouvernent" (Stock, 1976)
a6784.speech: Cited as the work to read to be convinced that the exercise of power and responsibility for a nation in the modern world cannot be borne over long years without the personality suffering and becoming subject to grave or even tragic errors.

a6784.speaker: Eleanor Roosevelt, wife of former US President Franklin D. Roosevelt
a6784.name: Eleanor Roosevelt
a6784.title: wife of former US President Franklin D. Roosevelt
a6784.speech: According to her, former president Franklin D. Roosevelt, who led the United States without interruption from March 1933 until his death in April 1945, no longer gave the affairs of state the care he had previously given them.

a6784.speaker: Corwin
a6784.name: Corwin
a6784.speech: Said that holding the highest office in a country is "a killing job".

a6784.speaker: Frère Melchior, author of "ICI, c'est le BENIN! (un peuple inattendument DEBOUT!)"
a6784.name: Frère Melchior
a6784.title: author of "ICI, c'est le BENIN! (un peuple inattendument DEBOUT!)"
a6784.speech: Asserted, less than a year ago on page 51, that Benin is the only country in the world whose constitution obliges the elected President of the Republic to swear an oath, before taking office, "before God, the Spirits of the Ancestors..., and before the People, sole holder of sovereignty".

a6784.speaker: Doyenne (most senior member) of the Beninese parliament
a6784.name: Doyenne (most senior member) of the Beninese parliament
a6784.speech: Affirmed within parliament itself that members of parliament are saleable and/or buyable.

a6992.speaker: A professor (unnamed, speaking at PhD orientation)
a6992.name: A professor (unnamed
a6992.title: speaking at PhD orientation)
a6992.speech: Warned that before we complete the course most of us shall have divorced.

a6992.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6992.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6992.speech: According to the WHO, depression affects 350 million people around the world and is the leading cause of disability globally.

a7091.speaker: Scientists
a7091.name: Scientists
a7091.speech: Warn that if the trend continues, Ghana could be forced to import clean water by 2030.

a7091.speaker: Rural dwellers and mining communities in Ghana
a7091.name: Rural dwellers and mining communities in Ghana
a7091.speech: Complain of strange illnesses linked to polluted water, while communities lament the loss of livelihoods.

a7091.speaker: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana (2017)
a7091.name: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo
a7091.title: President of Ghana (2017)
a7091.speech: Declared that he was ready to "put his presidency on the line" to fight galamsey, leading to the creation of the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Illegal Mining (IMCIM).

a7091.speaker: National Democratic Congress (NDC), opposition party
a7091.name: National Democratic Congress (NDC)
a7091.title: opposition party
a7091.speech: Accused the ruling New Patriotic Party (NPP) of failing to protect Ghana's environment.

a7091.speaker: Many analysts
a7091.name: Many analysts
a7091.speech: Believe Ghana cannot win this war through military crackdowns alone. They argue that solutions must be multidimensional: environmental agencies must be properly resourced and empowered to prosecute offenders without fear or favour; corruption, both in government and within traditional authority structures, must be tackled decisively; alternative livelihoods are essential; public awareness campaigns must be intensified, and technology such as drones and satellite mapping should be deployed to monitor illegal mining sites more effectively.

a7120.speaker: OCHA (humanitarian snapshot report)
a7120.name: OCHA (humanitarian snapshot report)
a7120.speech: Reported that June 2025 witnessed a deepening humanitarian crisis across Northern Mozambique, with escalating conflict, funding shortfalls, cholera outbreaks and the aftermath of three consecutive cyclones severely constraining humanitarian efforts; that humanitarian funding declined 26 per cent from $74 million in 2024 to $55 million (May 2025) and implementing partners fell 36 per cent from 76 to 49, leaving some 260,000 people without access to WASH services and 200,000 without adequate shelter and NFIs, while the laboratory sample collection program serving 250,000 individuals monthly, primarily those with HIV and TB, has been abruptly halted.

a7120.speaker: First assessments conducted since March in Lalaua and Muecate districts, Nampula
a7120.name: First assessments conducted since March in Lalaua and Muecate districts
a7120.title: Nampula
a7120.speech: Revealed that a combined 70,000 people were affected by the cyclones but have not received assistance since March, and noted severe infrastructure damage including a destroyed maternity ward that delivers an average of 136 births per month, and 117 unrepaired schools impacting 108,000 students.

a7120.speaker: Human Rights Watch
a7120.name: Human Rights Watch
a7120.speech: According to Human Rights Watch, about 120 children were abducted in Cabo Delgado since May and are forced into labor, early marriage or combat roles.

a7120.speaker: WFP 2025 Lean Season Assessment in Cabo Delgado
a7120.name: WFP 2025 Lean Season Assessment in Cabo Delgado
a7120.speech: According to WFP's 2025 Lean Season Assessment in Cabo Delgado, 80 per cent of households identify food as their top priority need; while overall food insecurity fell from 65 per cent in 2024 to 53 per cent in 2025, the impact of cyclones especially in Chiure, Mecufi, Pemba and Metuge remains severe, highlighting the urgent need for scaled-up support.

a7170.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a7170.name: Daniel Chapo
a7170.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a7170.speech: Reaffirmed on Wednesday (30-04) in Maputo that the country intends to consolidate bilateral relations with the United States of America (USA).

a7170.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a7170.name: Peter Hendrick Vrooman
a7170.title: US Ambassador to Mozambique
a7170.speech: Said the US administration will strengthen the partnership between the two countries, in the search for new opportunities in the private sector and US investments in strategic areas, citing the example of gas, health and infrastructure ; “There are 50 years of cooperation and partnerships between Mozambique and the United States of America” ; He stressed the importance of the US investing almost five billion dollars in the natural gas sector ; “Investment in roads, bridges, and other infrastructure areas is very important for the country’s economic growth.” ; Highlighted the importance of the Mozambican private sector in working together with the American private sector and other countries, as a basis for sustainable economic growth.

a7170.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a7170.name: Peter Hendrick Vrooman
a7170.title: US Ambassador to Mozambique
a7170.speech: “We talked about the possibility of continuing some projects, the importance of the US President’s AIDS Relief Program (PEPFAR), a program that saves the lives of many people in the country.” ; Guaranteed the continuity of this initiative, which has benefited many Mozambicans ; “I also mentioned the continuation of some programs that we have in the area of humanitarian assistance, which continues, but we also talked about the challenges.”

a7170.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a7170.name: Peter Hendrick Vrooman
a7170.title: US Ambassador to Mozambique
a7170.speech: Encouraged the Mozambican Head of State in his optimism, vision and resilience: “I think his optimism is very important, as the national anthem says, stone by stone building the new day. And this idea, I think we will work towards this and we are together.”

a7170.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a7170.name: Peter Hendrick Vrooman
a7170.title: US Ambassador to Mozambique
a7170.speech: Said that his mission as a diplomat was over, but relations between the two countries would continue.

a7245.speaker: Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed, Prime Minister of Djibouti
a7245.name: Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed
a7245.title: Prime Minister of Djibouti
a7245.speech: For his part gave priority in the discussions to the management of water resources through the desalination plant and to wind energy for agriculture in the north ; stressed the importance of economic cooperation, seeking investment and the know-how of American companies in order to acquire carbon-free energy through the development of solar power, geothermal energy and tidal power (a study financed from own funds on power generation at the Ghoubet strait was presented to the Ambassador), and now hydrogen.

a7245.speaker: Cynthia Kierscht, new Ambassador of the United States to Djibouti
a7245.name: Cynthia Kierscht
a7245.title: new Ambassador of the United States to Djibouti
a7245.speech: For her part pledged, with Djibouti's assistance, to promote Djibouti with the aim of boosting direct investment as well as trade between the United States and Djibouti, recalling that Djibouti hosts the largest American military base in Africa.

a7245.speaker: Denisa-Elena Ionete, new Ambassador of the European Union to Djibouti
a7245.name: Denisa-Elena Ionete
a7245.title: new Ambassador of the European Union to Djibouti
a7245.speech: Underlined the importance of maintaining regular meetings with the Prime Minister in order to strengthen collaboration and ensure a continuous dialogue focused on Djibouti's priorities and needs ; stressed a regional approach to meeting the challenges, notably maritime security in the Bab al-Mandeb, an increasingly disrupted area, which affects global maritime trade.

a7333.speaker: Brian Shukan, US Ambassador to Benin
a7333.name: Brian Shukan
a7333.title: US Ambassador to Benin
a7333.speech: Recalled that the partnership between his country and Benin is founded on shared values, notably a commitment to democracy, sustainable development, economic opportunity, security cooperation and the strengthening of ties between the two peoples. "We appreciate our productive partnership with the government of President Patrice Talon to develop economic opportunities and the well-being of all Beninese." ; Cited as examples the achievements of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) since 2016 – access to land, justice and financial services, modernisation of the port of Cotonou, access to energy and the improvement of the Benin-Niger corridor whose compact was signed recently; also recalled the achievements of the United States Agency for International Development in the fight against malaria and tropical diseases, in improving maternal, neonatal and child health and family planning, and its work in water, sanitation and hygiene, good governance, human rights and social cohesion; and reported on the work of Peace Corps volunteers in Benin over 55 years, the US African Development Foundation, cooperation with the Beninese security and defence forces, the Ambassador's Special Self-Help Fund and US-sponsored professional and cultural exchange programmes.

a7333.speaker: Erick Jean-Marie Zinsou, Secretary General of Benin's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a7333.name: Erick Jean-Marie Zinsou
a7333.title: Secretary General of Benin's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a7333.speech: Endorsed the ambassador's remarks by returning to some of the achievements, actions and programmes of the United States in Benin, and conveyed the Beninese executive's gratitude to the American government and people; regarding the achievements of MCA-Benin II, assured the American partner that arrangements have been made to ensure their sustainability; concerning the regional compact, recalled that the terms for finalising the new compact are being finalised, ultimately to boost the Beninese economy.

a7486.speaker: Appeal Court of Lesotho (ruling)
a7486.name: Appeal Court of Lesotho (ruling)
a7486.speech: Ruled in favour of the individual whose lease had been issued first, in a high-profile feud involving two people holding leases to the same piece of land in Koalabata; the matter ended with the demolition of a house.

a7486.speaker: Tankiso Sephoso, Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.name: Tankiso Sephoso
a7486.title: Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.speech: “The LAA was established as part of a reform in the land sector during the Millennium Challenge Compact I, a partnership between the governments of Lesotho and the United States aimed at stimulating economic activity. It was recognized that Lesotho was underutilizing its land as an asset for development. Before the LAA, the Land Survey and Physical Planning (LSPP) department struggled with inefficiencies, corruption, and a lack of transparency in issuing leases. It could take over a year to obtain a lease, which made it difficult for individuals to use land as collateral or sublease it. Our primary goal is to issue leases efficiently. Within two years of LAA’s establishment, we reduced the waiting time for leases from 365 days to 30 days. Today, it takes between 15 and 20 days to issue a lease. We also register all land transactions, including subleasing and subdivision, and advise the government on land policies. Additionally, we mediate land disputes, particularly those involving leases.”

a7486.speaker: Tankiso Sephoso, Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.name: Tankiso Sephoso
a7486.title: Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.speech: On the process of applying for a lease: “According to the Land Act, land must be allocated by the local council, and the land must have been surveyed and planned beforehand. Councils are responsible for maintaining records of available and allocated sites within their jurisdiction. Once a council allocates land, it issues an allocation title or minutes. With this title, an identity document, and an S10 form, the individual can apply for a lease. LAA provides a list of registered land surveyors to assist with the land survey. After the survey is completed, LAA inspects the site to ensure the boundaries are correct and comply with regulations. Once approved, the S10 form is issued, and the lease is granted within 15 to 20 days.”

a7486.speaker: Tankiso Sephoso, Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.name: Tankiso Sephoso
a7486.title: Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.speech: On agricultural land sold for residential purposes: “If the land in question does not have a lease, the council has the authority to regulate its use. Councils should have physical planners who ensure compliance with land use regulations and prevent agricultural land from being converted for other purposes. If an individual applies for a lease and submits all the required documents, the LAA will issue a lease. However, it is the council’s responsibility to ensure compliance with land use laws before approving land allocation.”

a7486.speaker: Tankiso Sephoso, Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.name: Tankiso Sephoso
a7486.title: Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.speech: On more than one person holding a lease for the same piece of land, as in the Koalabata case: “One of the reasons LAA was established was to prevent such issues by ensuring our systems detect errors, such as encroachments or overlapping surveys. Some cases predate the formation of LAA and require further review. Currently, it is impossible for more than one person to hold a lease for the same piece of land. However, technical errors can occur, such as issuing the same lease number for different plots. These errors are easily detected and corrected.”

a7486.speaker: Tankiso Sephoso, Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.name: Tankiso Sephoso
a7486.title: Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.speech: On whether the LAA is operating at full capacity: “As a parastatal with operational autonomy, we develop three-year strategic plans and annual business and operational plans. These help us prioritize and measure our performance. While we are generally doing well, there is room for improvement, especially in financial management.”

a7486.speaker: Tankiso Sephoso, Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.name: Tankiso Sephoso
a7486.title: Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Corporate Services
a7486.speech: On challenges facing the land sector: “There are too many actors in the land sector, some of whom are unregulated. Various institutions, such as Lesotho Housing, LNDC, LAA, councils, and the Commissioner of Lands, all have regulations, but better coordination between them could enhance efficiency in the sector.”

a7520.speaker: Johannes !Gawaxab, Bank of Namibia Governor
a7520.name: Johannes !Gawaxab
a7520.title: Bank of Namibia Governor
a7520.speech: Highlighted the emergence of a new world order, defined by evolving geopolitical developments, intensified trade tensions and rapid technological advancement; noted that these new global dynamics are challenging traditional frameworks around globalisation, multilateralism and market openness, and called for enhanced institutional agility and strategic foresight. "Although it is impossible to predict the future with certainty, the combined speed of these changes underscores the necessity for institutions, such as central banks, to continue to serve as guardians of stability in an environment characterised by volatility. As a central bank, we remain anchored to our mandate of price stability and financial stability."

a7520.speaker: Johannes !Gawaxab, Bank of Namibia Governor
a7520.name: Johannes !Gawaxab
a7520.title: Bank of Namibia Governor
a7520.speech: Reiterated the institution's commitment to building a smart central bank, fostering an inclusive and resilient financial system and embracing a new economy; highlighted key reform initiatives, including the establishment of Namibia's first Central Securities Depository to modernise financial markets as well as the launch of the Instant Payment Programme.

a7520.speaker: Johannes !Gawaxab, Bank of Namibia Governor
a7520.name: Johannes !Gawaxab
a7520.title: Bank of Namibia Governor
a7520.speech: Welcomed the diplomatic community, expressing gratitude for their continued interest in the Bank's work.

a7520.speaker: Bank of Namibia (economic presentation)
a7520.name: Bank of Namibia (economic presentation)
a7520.speech: Pointed out that the global economy is projected to grow at a subdued pace of 2.8% in 2025 and 3% in 2026, amid continued volatility in trade and financial markets; BoN expects domestic economic growth to improve moderately to 3.8% in 2025, rising slightly to 4% in 2026, driven by improved performance in the agriculture, non-diamond mining sector, electricity and water as well as construction, despite external pressures such as global price declines in diamonds and the potential impact of tariffs on some exports.

a7520.speaker: Johannes !Gawaxab, Bank of Namibia Governor
a7520.name: Johannes !Gawaxab
a7520.title: Bank of Namibia Governor
a7520.speech: Noted that domestic inflation remains well-contained, supported by the central bank's prudent monetary policy stance: "The policy interest rate has been reduced by a cumulative 100 basis points since August 2024, contributing to a marked decline in inflation from 5.4% in January 2024 to 3.6% in April 2025." ; Noted that the banking sector continued to demonstrate resilience, with sufficient capital buffers and liquidity to absorb shocks and support credit extension to the real economy.
